title.en: Volume 134 Biographies 84: Ma Sui, Hun Jian

sentences.zh: 馬燧

translations.literal: Ma Sui
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui

sentences.zh: 馬燧，字洵美，汝州郟城人，其先自右扶風徙焉。

translations.literal: Ma Sui, styled Xunmei, was a native of Jia County in Ru Prefecture; his ancestors had moved there from You Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui, styled Xunmei, was a native of Jia County in Ru Prefecture. His ancestors had moved there from You Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 祖瑉，官至左玉鈐衛倉曹。

translations.literal: His grandfather Min reached the office of Left Jade Bell Guard granary clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Min rose to the post of granary clerk in the Left Jade Bell Guard.

sentences.zh: 父季龍，嘗舉明《孫》《吳》，俶儻善兵法，官至嵐州刺史、幽州經略軍使。

translations.literal: His father Jilong once passed the Ming examination in Sun and Wu, was bold and unconventional and skilled in military strategy, and reached the offices of Lan Prefecture prefect and Youzhou frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jilong had once passed the Ming examination in the Sunzi and Wuzi; bold and unconventional, he excelled at military strategy and rose to prefect of Lan Prefecture and commissioner of the Youzhou frontier.

sentences.zh: 燧少時，嘗與諸兄讀書，乃輟卷嘆曰：「天下將有事矣，丈夫當建功於代，以濟四海，安能矻矻為一儒哉！」

translations.literal: When Sui was young, he once read with his elder brothers, then laid down the scroll and sighed, saying: "The empire will soon know turmoil; a man ought to build merit in his age to aid all under Heaven—how can he drudge on as a mere scholar!"
translations.idiomatic: In youth Ma Sui was reading with his elder brothers when he laid down the scroll and sighed: "Trouble is coming to the empire. A man ought to build merit in his age to aid all under Heaven—how can he drudge on as a mere scholar!"

sentences.zh: 燧姿度魁異，長六尺二寸，沈勇多智略，該涉群書，尤善兵法。

translations.literal: Sui's bearing was unusually imposing; he stood six feet two inches, was deep and brave with many stratagems, versed in many books, and especially skilled in military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui's bearing was unusually imposing. Six feet two inches tall, he was deep-spirited and brave, rich in stratagems, widely read, and especially skilled in the art of war.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，俾光祿卿賈循守范陽。

translations.literal: When An Lushu rebelled, he ordered Vice Director of Imperial Banquets Jia Xun to hold Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushu rebelled, he ordered Vice Director of Imperial Banquets Jia Xun to hold Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 燧說循曰：「祿山負恩首亂，雖陷洛城，必當夷滅。

translations.literal: Sui said to Xun: "Lushu has betrayed grace and risen first in rebellion; though he has taken Luoyang, he will surely be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui said to Jia Xun, "Lushu has betrayed the grace shown him and risen first in rebellion. Though he has taken Luoyang, he will surely be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 公盍建不代之功，誅其逆將向潤客、牛廷玠，拔其根柢，祿山西不能入關，則坐而受擒，天下可定也。」

translations.literal: Why do you not establish a merit no age can surpass—execute his rebellious generals Xiang Runkhe and Niu Tingjie, uproot his foundation; then Lushu cannot enter the passes from the west and will be captured sitting still, and the empire can be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Why not establish a merit no age can surpass—execute his rebellious generals Xiang Runkhe and Niu Tingjie and uproot his foundation? Then Lushu cannot enter the passes from the west and will be captured sitting still, and the empire can be settled."

sentences.zh: 循雖善之，計不時決，事泄，祿山果遣韓朝陽來召循。

translations.literal: Though Xun approved, he could not decide in time; the plan leaked, and Lushu indeed sent Han Chaoyang to summon Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xun approved the plan but could not decide in time. The scheme leaked, and Lushu did send Han Chaoyang to summon him.

sentences.zh: 朝陽至范陽，與循語，陰伏壯士以弓弦縊殺之。

translations.literal: When Chaoyang reached Fanyang and spoke with Xun, Sui secretly posted strong men who strangled him with bowstrings.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Chaoyang reached Fanyang and spoke with Jia Xun, Ma Sui secretly posted strong men who strangled him with bowstrings.

sentences.zh: 燧脫身走西山，隱者徐遇匿之。

translations.literal: Sui escaped to the Western Hills; the recluse Xu Yu hid him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui escaped to the Western Hills, where the recluse Xu Yu hid him.

sentences.zh: 逾月，間行歸平原。

translations.literal: After more than a month he traveled by hidden routes back to Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he made his way back to Pingyuan by hidden routes.

sentences.zh: 平原不守，復走魏郡。

translations.literal: When Pingyuan could not be held, he fled again to Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingyuan could not be held, he fled again to Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，澤潞節度使李抱玉署奏趙城尉。

translations.literal: In the Baoying era, Ze-Lu military commissioner Li Baoyu appointed and memorialized him as assistant magistrate of Zhao City.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoying era, Ze-Lu military commissioner Li Baoyu appointed and memorialized him assistant magistrate of Zhao City.

sentences.zh: 是時回紇大軍還國，恃復東都之功，倔強恣睢，所過或虜掠廩粟，供餼小不如意，恣行殺害。

translations.literal: At that time the Uyghur great army was returning home, relying on its merit in recovering the Eastern Capital; arrogant and overbearing, wherever it passed it sometimes plundered granary grain, and if supplies were the least unsatisfactory it killed at will.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Uyghur great army was returning home, swaggering over its merit in recovering the Eastern Capital. Wherever it passed it sometimes plundered granary grain, and if supplies were the least unsatisfactory it killed at will.

sentences.zh: 抱玉具供辦，賓介皆憚不敢行，燧自贊請主郵驛。

translations.literal: Baoyu fully prepared provisions, yet his staff all feared to go; Sui volunteered to take charge of the courier stations.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu fully prepared provisions, yet none of his staff dared go. Ma Sui volunteered to take charge of the courier stations.

sentences.zh: 比回紇至，則先賂其渠帥，與明要約，回紇乃授燧旗幟為識，犯令者命燧戮之。

translations.literal: When the Uyghurs arrived, he first bribed their chieftains and made clear agreements with them; the Uyghurs then gave Sui banners and flags as tokens, and whoever violated the orders was executed on Sui's authority.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs arrived, he first bribed their chieftains and made explicit agreements with them. The Uyghurs then gave Ma Sui banners and flags as tokens, and anyone who violated the orders was executed on his authority.

sentences.zh: 取死囚給左右廝役，小違令，輒殺之。

translations.literal: He took condemned prisoners and gave them to his attendants as servants; at the slightest breach of orders he killed them.
translations.idiomatic: He took condemned prisoners and assigned them as attendants; at the slightest breach of orders he killed them.

sentences.zh: 回紇相顧失色，虜涉其境，無敢暴掠。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs looked at one another and paled; the tribesmen who crossed his territory dared not plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs looked at one another and paled. Tribesmen who crossed his territory dared not plunder.

sentences.zh: 抱玉益奇之。

translations.literal: Baoyu admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 燧因說抱玉曰：「屬者與回紇言，燧得其情。

translations.literal: Sui then said to Baoyu: "When I spoke with the Uyghurs recently, Sui learned their mind.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then said to Li Baoyu, "When I spoke with the Uyghurs recently, I learned their mind.

sentences.zh: 今仆固懷恩恃功樹黨，李懷仙、張忠誌、薛嵩、田承嗣分授疆土，皆出於懷恩，其子瑒佻勇不義。

translations.literal: Now Pugu Huai'en relies on merit and builds factions; Li Huaixian, Zhang Zhongzhi, Xue Song, and Tian Chengsi were each granted territory—all through Huai'en—and his son Yang is frivolous, brave, and unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: Now Pugu Huai'en relies on his merit and builds factions. Li Huaixian, Zhang Zhongzhi, Xue Song, and Tian Chengsi were each granted territory—all through Huai'en—and his son Yang is frivolous, brave, and unrighteous.

sentences.zh: 以燧度之，將必窺太原西山以為亂，公宜深備之。」

translations.literal: By Sui's estimate he will surely watch for an opening on the Western Hills of Taiyuan to raise rebellion; you should prepare deeply against it."
translations.idiomatic: By my estimate he will surely watch for an opening on the Western Hills of Taiyuan to raise rebellion. You should prepare deeply against it."

sentences.zh: 無何，懷恩果與太原都將李竭誠通謀，將取太原，其帥辛雲京覺之，斬竭誠，固城自守，懷恩遣其子瑒率兵圍之。

translations.literal: Before long Huai'en did conspire with Taiyuan garrison commander Li Jiecheng; intending to take Taiyuan, its commander Xin Yunjing detected it, executed Jiecheng, and held the city; Huai'en sent his son Yang to lead troops and besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huai'en did conspire with Taiyuan garrison commander Li Jiecheng to take Taiyuan. Commander Xin Yunjing detected the plot, executed Jiecheng, and held the city. Huai'en sent his son Yang to lead troops and besiege it.

sentences.zh: 初，回紇北歸，遣其將安恪、石常庭將兵數百及誘募附麗者復數千人以守河陽，東都所虜掠重貨，悉積河陽。

translations.literal: At first, as the Uyghurs returned north they left their generals An Ke and Shi Changting with several hundred troops, plus several thousand more recruited and attached men, to hold Heyang; the heavy goods plundered in the Eastern Capital were all stored at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as the Uyghurs returned north they left their generals An Ke and Shi Changting with several hundred troops, plus several thousand more recruited and attached men, to hold Heyang. The heavy goods plundered in the Eastern Capital were all stored at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 是時，懷恩遺薛嵩自相、衛饋糧以絕河津。

translations.literal: At that time Huai'en had Xue Song supply grain from Xiang and Wei to cut the river crossings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huai'en had Xue Song supply grain from Xiang and Wei to cut the river crossings.

sentences.zh: 抱玉令燧詣薛嵩說之，嵩乃絕懷恩從順。

translations.literal: Baoyu ordered Sui to go persuade Xue Song; Song then broke with Huai'en and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu ordered Ma Sui to go persuade Xue Song. Song then broke with Huai'en and submitted.

sentences.zh: 署奏左武衛兵曹。

translations.literal: He was appointed and memorialized as Left Martial Guard army clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed and memorialized Left Martial Guard army clerk.

sentences.zh: 歷太子通事舍人，遷著作郎、營田判官。

translations.literal: He served as Crown Prince's attendant and memorial envoy, then was transferred to drafting editor and garrison-fields judge.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Crown Prince's attendant and memorial envoy, then was transferred to drafting editor and garrison-fields judge.

sentences.zh: 無幾，遷秘書少監、兼殿中侍御史，為節度判官、承務郎，遷鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat and concurrently palace censor, became military commissioner's judge and officer of court service, and was promoted to prefect of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat and concurrently palace censor, served as the military commissioner's judge and officer of court service, and was promoted to prefect of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 燧乃勸課農畝，總其戶籍，歲一稅之，州人以為便。

translations.literal: Sui then encouraged farming, consolidated household registers, and taxed once a year; the people of the prefecture found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then encouraged farming, consolidated household registers, and taxed once a year. The people of the prefecture found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 大歷四年，改懷州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dali he was transferred to prefect of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dali he was transferred to prefect of Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乘亂兵之後，其夏大旱，人失耕稼；

translations.literal: After the chaos of war that summer there was great drought and people lost their planting and harvest;
translations.idiomatic: After the chaos of war that summer there was great drought, and people lost their planting and harvest.

sentences.zh: 燧乃務修教化，將吏有父母者，燧輒造之施敬，收葬暴骨，去其煩苛。

translations.literal: Sui then devoted himself to teaching and transforming the people; wherever officers had parents, Sui would visit them to show respect, gathered and buried exposed bones, and removed harsh regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then devoted himself to teaching and transforming the people. Wherever officers had parents, he would visit them to show respect; he gathered and buried exposed bones and removed harsh regulations.

sentences.zh: 至秋，界中生魯谷，人頗賴之。

translations.literal: By autumn millet sprouted in the district and people relied on it greatly.
translations.idiomatic: By autumn millet sprouted in the district, and the people relied on it greatly.

sentences.zh: 抱玉移鎮鳳翔，以汧陽被邊，署奏隴州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Baoyu moved his command to Fengxiang, because Qianyang lay on the frontier he was appointed and memorialized prefect of Long Prefecture and concurrently censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baoyu moved his command to Fengxiang, because Qianyang lay on the frontier Ma Sui was appointed and memorialized prefect of Long Prefecture and concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 州西有通道，廣二百余步，上連峻山，山與吐蕃相直，虜每入寇，皆出於此。

translations.literal: West of the prefecture was a passage more than two hundred paces wide, joining steep mountains that faced Tibet directly; whenever the barbarians raided they came out by this route.
translations.idiomatic: West of the prefecture was a passage more than two hundred paces wide, joining steep mountains that faced Tibet directly. Whenever the barbarians raided, they came out by this route.

sentences.zh: 燧乃按行險易，立石種樹以塞之，下置二門，設籬櫓，八日而功畢。

translations.literal: Sui then inspected the terrain's advantages and difficulties, set up stones and planted trees to block it, placed two gates below and set palisades and watchtowers; the work was finished in eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then inspected the terrain's advantages and difficulties, set up stones and planted trees to block the passage, placed two gates below, and set palisades and watchtowers. The work was finished in eight days.

sentences.zh: 會抱玉入覲，與燧俱行。

translations.literal: When Baoyu went to court he went together with Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baoyu went to court, Ma Sui went with him.

sentences.zh: 久之，代宗知其能，召見，拜商州刺史、兼御史中丞、防禦水陸運使。

translations.literal: After a long time Daizong learned of his ability, summoned him, and appointed him prefect of Shang Prefecture, concurrently censor-in-chief and commissioner for land and water transport defense.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time Emperor Daizong learned of his ability, summoned him, and appointed him prefect of Shang Prefecture, concurrently censor-in-chief and commissioner for land and water transport defense.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年，河陽三城兵亂，逐鎮將常休明，以燧檢校左散騎常侍、御史大夫、河陽三城使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dali the three-city garrison of Heyang mutinied, drove out garrison commander Chang Xiuming, and Sui was made acting minister of works, censor-in-chief, and commissioner of the three cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Dali the three-city garrison of Heyang mutinied, drove out garrison commander Chang Xiuming, and Ma Sui was made acting minister of works, censor-in-chief, and commissioner of the three cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月，汴州大將李靈耀反，因據州城，絕運路，以邀節制。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year the great general of Bian Prefecture Li Lingyao rebelled, seized the prefectural city, cut the transport routes, and sought to extort the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eleventh year the great general of Bian Prefecture, Li Lingyao, rebelled, seized the prefectural city, cut the transport routes, and sought to extort the military commission.

sentences.zh: 代宗務姑息人，因授靈耀汴、宋等八州節度留後。

translations.literal: Daizong, intent on indulgence, therefore appointed Lingyao acting military commissioner of the eight prefectures of Bian, Song, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong, intent on indulgence, therefore appointed Lingyao acting military commissioner of the eight prefectures of Bian, Song, and others.

sentences.zh: 靈耀不受命。

translations.literal: Lingyao did not accept the order.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingyao did not accept the order.

sentences.zh: 乃潛結魏博；

translations.literal: He then secretly allied with Weibo;
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly allied with Weibo.

sentences.zh: 田承嗣乃遣兄子悅將兵援靈耀，破永平軍將劉洽。

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi sent his nephew's son Yue to lead troops to aid Lingyao and defeated Yongping Army commander Liu Qia.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi sent his nephew's son Yue to lead troops to aid Lingyao and defeated Yongping Army commander Liu Qia.

sentences.zh: 詔燧與淮西節度使李忠臣合軍討靈耀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sui and Huai Prefecture military commissioner Li Zhongchen to join armies and attack Lingyao.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Ma Sui and Huai Prefecture military commissioner Li Zhongchen to join armies and attack Lingyao.

sentences.zh: 忠臣懼賊，焚廬舍西走。

translations.literal: Zhongchen feared the bandits and burned his quarters and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen feared the bandits, burned his quarters, and fled west.

sentences.zh: 燧勸其還兵，請為前鋒，擊破田悅，進逼汴州。

translations.literal: Sui urged him to return his troops, asked to serve as vanguard, defeated Tian Yue, and pressed on toward Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui urged him to return his troops, asked to serve as vanguard, defeated Tian Yue, and pressed on toward Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 忠臣行汴南，燧引軍行汴北，又敗靈耀將張清於西梁固。

translations.literal: Zhongchen marched south of Bian; Sui led his army north of Bian and again defeated Lingyao's general Zhang Qing at Xilianggu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen marched south of Bian. Ma Sui led his army north of Bian and again defeated Lingyao's general Zhang Qing at Xilianggu.

sentences.zh: 靈耀選銳兵八千，號為「餓狼軍」；

translations.literal: Lingyao selected eight thousand elite troops and called them the "Starving Wolf Army";
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingyao selected eight thousand elite troops and called them the "Starving Wolf Army."

sentences.zh: 燧獨引軍擊破之，進至浚儀。

translations.literal: Sui alone led his army, defeated them, and advanced to Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui alone led his army, defeated them, and advanced to Junyi.

sentences.zh: 是時，河陽兵冠諸軍。

translations.literal: At that time the Heyang troops were foremost among the armies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Heyang troops were foremost among the armies.

sentences.zh: 承嗣又遣悅將兵二萬救靈耀，破永平軍將杜如江，略曹州，又敗李正己遊軍，擊走劉洽、長孫全緒等軍，乘勝去汴州一舍，方陣而進。

translations.literal: Chengsi again sent Yue with twenty thousand troops to rescue Lingyao; he defeated Yongping Army commander Du Rujiang, raided Cao Prefecture, again defeated Li Zhengyi's roaming troops, drove off the armies of Liu Qia and Zhangsun Quanxu and others, and in victory advanced to within one stage of Bian Prefecture, advancing in square formation.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi again sent Yue with twenty thousand troops to rescue Lingyao. He defeated Yongping Army commander Du Rujiang, raided Cao Prefecture, again defeated Li Zhengyi's roaming troops, drove off the armies of Liu Qia and Zhangsun Quanxu and others, and in victory advanced to within one stage of Bian Prefecture, advancing in square formation.

sentences.zh: 忠臣會宋州、淮南、浙西兵，與戰不利，請救於燧，燧引四千人為奇兵擊破之，田悅匹馬遁去。

translations.literal: Zhongchen joined troops from Song Prefecture, Huainan, and Zhexi and fought without success; he asked Sui for rescue, and Sui led four thousand men as a surprise force and defeated them; Tian Yue fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen joined troops from Song Prefecture, Huainan, and Zhexi and fought without success. He asked Ma Sui for rescue, and Sui led four thousand men as a surprise force and defeated them. Tian Yue fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 靈耀知悅敗，明日以百騎夜走，汴州悉降，燧讓功於忠臣。

translations.literal: When Lingyao learned Yue was defeated, the next day he fled by night with a hundred horsemen; Bian Prefecture fully surrendered, and Sui yielded the merit to Zhongchen.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingyao learned Yue was defeated, the next day he fled by night with a hundred horsemen. Bian Prefecture fully surrendered, and Ma Sui yielded the merit to Li Zhongchen.

sentences.zh: 忠臣素暴戾，燧不欲入汴城，乃引軍退舍於板橋。

translations.literal: Zhongchen had always been brutal and overbearing; Sui did not wish to enter Bian city and withdrew his army to camp at Banqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen had always been brutal and overbearing. Ma Sui did not wish to enter Bian city and withdrew his army to camp at Banqiao.

sentences.zh: 忠臣入城，果專其功，因會擊殺宋州刺史李僧惠。

translations.literal: When Zhongchen entered the city he indeed monopolized the merit and, at a gathering, killed Song Prefecture prefect Li Senghui.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhongchen entered the city he indeed monopolized the merit and, at a gathering, killed Song Prefecture prefect Li Senghui.

sentences.zh: 燧還河陽。

translations.literal: Sui returned to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui returned to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年六月，檢校工部尚書、太原尹、北都留守、河東節度留後，尋為節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Dali he was made acting minister of works, governor of Taiyuan, northern capital regent, and acting military commissioner of Hedong, and soon became military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Dali he was made acting minister of works, governor of Taiyuan, northern capital regent, and acting military commissioner of Hedong, and soon became military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太原承前政鮑防百井敗軍之後，兵甲寡弱，燧乃悉召將吏牧馬廝役，得數千人，悉補騎卒，教之數月，為精騎。

translations.literal: Taiyuan, after the defeat of Bao Fang's Baibing army under the previous administration, had weak arms and armor; Sui then summoned officers, grooms, and servants and got several thousand men, all filled out as cavalry, trained them for months, and made elite horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan, after the defeat of Bao Fang's Baibing army under the previous administration, had weak arms and armor. Ma Sui then summoned officers, grooms, and servants and got several thousand men, all filled out as cavalry. After months of training they became elite horsemen.

sentences.zh: 造甲者必令長短三等，稱其所衣，以便進趨。

translations.literal: Those who made armor had to make three grades of length, matched to what the wearer wore, for ease in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Those who made armor had to make three grades of length, matched to what the wearer wore, for ease in advance.

sentences.zh: 又造戰車，蒙以狻猊象，列戟於後，行則載兵甲，止則為營陣，或塞險以遏奔沖，器械無不犀利。

translations.literal: He also made war chariots covered with suanni figures, with halberds arrayed behind; marching they carried arms and armor, halting they formed camp formations, or blocked narrow passes to check rushing charges—the implements were all sharp and effective.
translations.idiomatic: He also made war chariots covered with suanni figures, with halberds arrayed behind. Marching they carried arms and armor; halting they formed camp formations, or blocked narrow passes to check rushing charges. The implements were all sharp and effective.

sentences.zh: 居一年，陳兵三萬，開廣場以習戰陣，教其進退坐作之勢。

translations.literal: After a year he arrayed thirty thousand troops, opened a broad field to practice battle formations, and taught the postures of advance, retreat, sitting, and rising.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he arrayed thirty thousand troops, opened a broad field to practice battle formations, and taught the postures of advance, retreat, sitting, and rising.

sentences.zh: 建中二年六月，朝於京師，加檢校兵部尚書，令還太原。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Jianzhong he attended court at the capital and was promoted acting minister of war, then ordered back to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Jianzhong he attended court at the capital, was promoted acting minister of war, and was ordered back to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，田悅新代承嗣統兵，恐人不附己，詐效誠款，燧上疏明其必反，宜先備之。

translations.literal: At first Tian Yue had newly succeeded Chengsi in command of the troops and feared men would not attach to him; he feigned sincere submission, and Sui memorialized clarifying that he would surely rebel and that one should prepare first.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tian Yue had newly succeeded Chengsi in command of the troops and feared men would not attach to him. He feigned sincere submission, and Ma Sui memorialized clarifying that he would surely rebel and that one should prepare first.

sentences.zh: 其年，悅果與淄青、恆冀通謀，自將兵三萬圍邢州，次臨洺，築重城，絕其內外，以拒救兵。

translations.literal: That year Yue indeed conspired with Ziqing and Hengji, personally led thirty thousand troops to besiege Xing Prefecture, halted at Linming, built a heavy wall, cut off inside and outside, and resisted rescue troops.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yue indeed conspired with Ziqing and Hengji, personally led thirty thousand troops to besiege Xing Prefecture, halted at Linming, built a heavy wall, cut off inside and outside, and resisted rescue troops.

sentences.zh: 邢州將李洪、臨洺將張伾，皆堅守不拔。

translations.literal: Xing Prefecture commander Li Hong and Linming commander Zhang Pi both held firm and could not be pulled down.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Prefecture commander Li Hong and Linming commander Zhang Pi both held firm and could not be pulled down.

sentences.zh: 昭義軍告急，乃詔燧將步騎二萬與昭義節度使李抱真、神策行營兵馬使李晟合軍救臨洺。

translations.literal: The Zhaoyi Army reported urgent distress; an edict then ordered Sui to lead twenty thousand foot and horse with Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Baozhen and Shence mobile-camp military envoy Li Sheng to join armies and rescue Linming.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhaoyi Army reported urgent distress. An edict then ordered Ma Sui to lead twenty thousand foot and horse with Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Baozhen and Shence mobile-camp military envoy Li Sheng to join armies and rescue Linming.

sentences.zh: 燧軍出郭口，兵未過險，乃遣持書喻悅，且示之好，悅謂燧畏之。

translations.literal: When Sui's army left Guokou the troops had not yet passed the dangerous ground; he sent a letter to persuade Yue and showed goodwill, and Yue thought Sui feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Sui's army left Guokou the troops had not yet passed the dangerous ground. He sent a letter to persuade Yue and showed goodwill, and Yue thought Sui feared him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，師次邯鄲，悅遣使至，燧皆斬之以徇；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the army halted at Handan; Yue sent envoys, and Sui beheaded them all to announce to the army;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the army halted at Handan. Yue sent envoys, and Ma Sui beheaded them all to announce to the army.

sentences.zh: 遣兵擊破其支軍，射殺其將成炫之。

translations.literal: he sent troops to defeat Yue's detached army and shot and killed his general Cheng Xuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to defeat Yue's detached army and shot and killed his general Cheng Xuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 悅自攻臨洺，遣大將楊朝光將兵萬人，於臨洺南雙岡東西列二柵以禦燧。

translations.literal: Yue personally attacked Linming and sent great general Yang Chaoguang with ten thousand troops south of Linming at Shuanggang to set up two palisades east and west to resist Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yue personally attacked Linming and sent great general Yang Chaoguang with ten thousand troops south of Linming at Shuanggang to set up two palisades east and west to resist Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 燧乃率李抱真、李晟進軍，營於二柵之中。

translations.literal: Sui then led Li Baozhen and Li Sheng forward, encamping between the two palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then led Li Baozhen and Li Sheng forward, encamping between the two palisades.

sentences.zh: 其夜，東柵走歸悅。

translations.literal: That night the eastern palisade fled back to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: That night the eastern palisade fled back to Yue.

sentences.zh: 明日，燧進軍營明山，取其棄柵以置輜重。

translations.literal: The next day Sui advanced and encamped at Mingshan, taking the abandoned palisade to place baggage.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ma Sui advanced and encamped at Mingshan, taking the abandoned palisade to place baggage.

sentences.zh: 悅謂將吏曰：「朝光堅柵不下萬人，假令燧等盡銳攻之，比數日，計不能下，殺傷必甚。

translations.literal: Yue said to his officers: "Chaoguang's strong palisade holds no fewer than ten thousand men; even if Sui and the others attack with full strength, in several days by estimate they cannot take it, and casualties must be heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said to his officers, "Chaoguang's strong palisade holds no fewer than ten thousand men. Even if Sui and the others attack with full strength, in several days by estimate they cannot take it, and casualties must be heavy.

sentences.zh: 吾此必拔臨洺，賞勞軍士而與之戰，必勝之術也。」

translations.literal: I shall surely take Linming here, reward and comfort the troops and fight them—that is the sure way to victory."
translations.idiomatic: I shall surely take Linming here, reward and comfort the troops, and fight them—that is the sure way to victory."

sentences.zh: 悅乃分恆州李惟嶽救兵五千以助朝光，燧率軍攻朝光，田悅將萬余人救之。

translations.literal: Yue then divided five thousand rescue troops from Heng Prefecture under Li Weiyue to aid Chaoguang; Sui led his army to attack Chaoguang, and Tian Yue led more than ten thousand men to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then divided five thousand rescue troops from Heng Prefecture under Li Weiyue to aid Chaoguang. Ma Sui led his army to attack Chaoguang, and Tian Yue led more than ten thousand men to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 燧乃令大將李自良、李奉國將騎兵合神策軍於雙岡禦之，令曰：「令悅得過，當斬爾！」

translations.literal: Sui then ordered great generals Li Ziliang and Li Fengguo to lead cavalry with the Shence Army at Shuanggang to resist them, commanding: "If Yue gets through, you shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then ordered great generals Li Ziliang and Li Fengguo to lead cavalry with the Shence Army at Shuanggang to resist them, commanding: "If Yue gets through, you shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 自良等擊卻悅。

translations.literal: Ziliang and the others beat Yue back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ziliang and the others beat Yue back.

sentences.zh: 燧乃令推火車以焚其柵，斬朝光及大將盧子昌，斬首五千余級，生虜八百余人。

translations.literal: Sui then ordered fire carts pushed to burn the palisade, beheaded Chaoguang and great general Lu Zichang, cut off more than five thousand heads, and captured more than eight hundred alive.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then ordered fire carts pushed to burn the palisade, beheaded Chaoguang and great general Lu Zichang, cut off more than five thousand heads, and captured more than eight hundred alive.

sentences.zh: 居五日，進軍至臨洺，田悅悉軍戰。

translations.literal: After five days he advanced to Linming; Tian Yue mustered his whole army to fight.
translations.idiomatic: After five days he advanced to Linming. Tian Yue mustered his whole army to fight.

sentences.zh: 燧自將銳兵扼其沖口，凡百余合，士皆決死，悅兵大敗，斬首萬余級，生虜九百人，得谷三十萬斛，器甲稱是。

translations.literal: Sui personally led elite troops to hold the crossing mouth; in more than a hundred engagements the men all fought to the death; Yue's troops were greatly defeated—more than ten thousand heads cut off, more than nine hundred captured alive, thirty thousand bushels of grain taken, and arms and armor in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui personally led elite troops to hold the crossing mouth. In more than a hundred engagements the men all fought to the death. Yue's troops were greatly defeated—more than ten thousand heads cut off, more than nine hundred captured alive, thirty thousand bushels of grain taken, and arms and armor in proportion.

sentences.zh: 悅收敗兵夜遁，邢州圍亦解。

translations.literal: Yue gathered defeated troops and fled by night; the siege of Xing Prefecture was also lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Yue gathered defeated troops and fled by night. The siege of Xing Prefecture was also lifted.

sentences.zh: 以功加右僕射。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was promoted right vice director.

sentences.zh: 先戰，燧誓軍中，戰勝請以家財行賞，既勝，盡出其私財以頒將士。

translations.literal: Before battle Sui had sworn in the army that if they won he would ask to reward them from his household wealth; once victorious he fully brought out his private wealth to distribute to officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: Before battle Ma Sui had sworn in the army that if they won he would ask to reward them from his household wealth. Once victorious he fully brought out his private wealth to distribute to officers and men.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，詔度支出錢五萬貫行賞，還燧家財。

translations.literal: Dezong praised this; an edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to disburse fifty thousand strings of cash for rewards and return Sui's household wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong praised this. An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to disburse fifty thousand strings of cash for rewards and return Ma Sui's household wealth.

sentences.zh: 尋加魏博招討使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Weibo pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Weibo pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，田悅求救於淄青、恆冀，李納遣大將衛俊將兵萬人救悅，李惟嶽亦遣兵三千赴援。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Tian Yue asked Ziqing and Hengji for rescue; Li Na sent great general Wei Jun with ten thousand troops to rescue Yue, and Li Weiyue also sent three thousand troops to aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Tian Yue asked Ziqing and Hengji for rescue. Li Na sent great general Wei Jun with ten thousand troops to rescue Yue, and Li Weiyue also sent three thousand troops to aid.

sentences.zh: 悅收合散卒二萬余人，壁於洹水，淄青軍其東，恆冀軍其西，首尾相應。

translations.literal: Yue gathered more than twenty thousand scattered troops and walled at the Huan River; Ziqing troops were on its east, Hengji troops on its west, head and tail responding to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yue gathered more than twenty thousand scattered troops and walled at the Huan River. Ziqing troops were on its east, Hengji troops on its west, head and tail responding to one another.

sentences.zh: 燧率諸軍進屯於鄴，奏請益河陽兵，詔河陽節度使李芃將兵會之。

translations.literal: Sui led the armies forward and encamped at Ye, memorialized asking to increase Heyang troops, and an edict ordered Heyang military commissioner Li Qi to lead troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui led the armies forward and encamped at Ye, memorialized asking to increase Heyang troops, and an edict ordered Heyang military commissioner Li Qi to lead troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 軍次於漳，悅遣將王光進以兵守長橋，築月城以為固，軍不得渡。

translations.literal: The army halted at Zhang; Yue sent general Wang Guangjin with troops to hold Changqiao and built a moon wall for solidity; the army could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Zhang. Yue sent general Wang Guangjin with troops to hold Changqiao and built a moon wall for solidity. The army could not cross.

sentences.zh: 燧乃於下流以車數百乘，維以鐵鎖，鎖絕中流，實以土囊以遏水，水稍淺，諸軍畢渡。

translations.literal: Sui then downstream used several hundred carts linked with iron chains, chains blocking midstream, filled with earth bags to check the water; when the water was somewhat shallow all the armies crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then downstream used several hundred carts linked with iron chains, chains blocking midstream, filled with earth bags to check the water. When the water was somewhat shallow all the armies crossed.

sentences.zh: 是時軍糧少，悅深壁不戰，欲老燧軍。

translations.literal: At that time army grain was scarce; Yue walled deeply and would not fight, intending to wear out Sui's army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time army grain was scarce. Yue walled deeply and would not fight, intending to wear out Ma Sui's army.

sentences.zh: 燧令諸軍持十日糧，進次倉口，與悅夾洹水而軍。

translations.literal: Sui ordered the armies to carry ten days' grain, advanced and halted at Cangkou, and encamped facing Yue across the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui ordered the armies to carry ten days' grain, advanced and halted at Cangkou, and encamped facing Yue across the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 抱真與李芃問：「糧少而深入，何也？」

translations.literal: Baozhen and Li Qi asked: "Grain is scarce yet you advance deeply—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen and Li Qi asked, "Grain is scarce yet you advance deeply—why?"

sentences.zh: 燧曰：「糧少利速戰，兵法善於致人，不致於人。

translations.literal: Sui said: "Scarce grain favors swift battle; in military strategy one excels at making others come, not at going to others.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui said, "Scarce grain favors swift battle. In military strategy one excels at making others come, not at going to others.

sentences.zh: 今田悅與淄青、恆三軍為首尾，計欲不戰，以老我師；

translations.literal: Now Tian Yue with Ziqing and Heng's three armies are head and tail; by plan they intend not to fight and to wear out our army;
translations.idiomatic: Now Tian Yue with Ziqing and Heng's three armies are head and tail. By plan they intend not to fight and to wear out our army.

sentences.zh: 若分軍擊其左右，兵少未可必破，悅且來救，是前後受敵也。

translations.literal: if we divide the army to strike their left and right, our troops are too few and victory cannot be assured; Yue will come to rescue and we will be attacked front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: If we divide the army to strike their left and right, our troops are too few and victory cannot be assured. Yue will come to rescue and we will be attacked front and rear.

sentences.zh: 兵法所謂攻其必救，彼固當戰也，燧為諸軍合而破之。」

translations.literal: What military strategy calls attacking where they must rescue—they surely will fight; Sui will join the armies and break them."
translations.idiomatic: What military strategy calls attacking where they must rescue—they surely will fight. I will join the armies and break them."

sentences.zh: 燧乃造三橋道逾洹水，日挑戰，悅不敢出。

translations.literal: Sui then built three bridge roads across the Huan River and challenged daily; Yue dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then built three bridge roads across the Huan River and challenged daily. Yue dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 恆州兵以軍少，懼為燧所並，引軍合於悅。

translations.literal: Heng Prefecture troops, because the army was small, feared being absorbed by Sui and led their army to join Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Prefecture troops, because the army was small, feared being absorbed by Ma Sui and led their army to join Yue.

sentences.zh: 悅謂燧明日復挑戰，乃伏兵萬人，欲邀燧。

translations.literal: Yue thought Sui would challenge again the next day and hid ten thousand troops intending to ambush Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yue thought Ma Sui would challenge again the next day and hid ten thousand troops intending to ambush him.

sentences.zh: 燧乃令諸軍半夜皆食，先雞鳴時擊鼓吹角，潛師傍洹水徑趨魏州，令曰：「聞賊至，則止為陣。」

translations.literal: Sui then ordered all armies to eat at midnight, before cockcrow beat drums, blow horns, and at the first cockcrow move troops secretly along the Huan River straight toward Wei Prefecture, commanding: "When you hear bandits arrive, halt and form battle lines."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then ordered all armies to eat at midnight, before cockcrow beat drums and blow horns, and at the first cockcrow move troops secretly along the Huan River straight toward Wei Prefecture, commanding: "When you hear bandits arrive, halt and form battle lines."

sentences.zh: 又令百騎吹鼓角，皆留於後，仍抱薪持火，待軍畢發，止鼓角匿其旁，伺悅軍畢渡，焚其橋。

translations.literal: He also ordered a hundred horsemen to blow horns and drums, all remaining behind, still carrying firewood and holding fire, waiting until the army finished crossing before lighting; then they stopped horns and drums and hid beside them, watching until Yue's army finished crossing and burned the bridges.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered a hundred horsemen to blow horns and drums, all remaining behind, still carrying firewood and holding fire, waiting until the army finished crossing before lighting. Then they stopped horns and drums and hid beside them, watching until Yue's army finished crossing and burned the bridges.

sentences.zh: 軍行十數里，悅乃率淄青、恆州步騎四萬余人逾橋掩其後，乘風縱火，鼓噪而進。

translations.literal: The army marched more than ten li; Yue then led more than forty thousand foot and horse of Ziqing and Heng Prefecture across the bridge to cover their rear, riding the wind to set fires, shouting and advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched more than ten li. Yue then led more than forty thousand foot and horse of Ziqing and Heng Prefecture across the bridge to cover their rear, riding the wind to set fires, shouting and advancing.

sentences.zh: 燧乃坐，申令無動，命前除草斬榛棘廣百步以為陣；

translations.literal: Sui then sat and ordered no movement, commanded those in front to clear grass and cut brambles a hundred paces wide to form battle lines;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then sat and ordered no movement, commanded those in front to clear grass and cut brambles a hundred paces wide to form battle lines.

sentences.zh: 燧出陣，募勇力得五千余人，分為前列，以俟賊至。

translations.literal: Sui came out of the lines, recruited the brave and strong and got more than five thousand men, divided them as the front rank, and waited for the bandits to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui came out of the lines, recruited the brave and strong and got more than five thousand men, divided them as the front rank, and waited for the bandits to arrive.

sentences.zh: 比悅軍至，則火止氣乏，力少衰，乃縱兵擊之，悅軍大敗。

translations.literal: When Yue's army arrived the fire stopped and their breath was spent, their strength somewhat faded; he then released troops to strike them and Yue's army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue's army arrived the fire stopped and their breath was spent, their strength somewhat faded. He then released troops to strike them and Yue's army was greatly defeated.

sentences.zh: 時神策、昭義、河陽軍小卻，河東軍既勝，諸軍還鬥，合擊又大破之。

translations.literal: At that time the Shence, Zhaoyi, and Heyang armies fell back slightly; once the Hedong army had won the other armies returned to fight, joined the strike, and again greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Shence, Zhaoyi, and Heyang armies fell back slightly. Once the Hedong army had won the other armies returned to fight, joined the strike, and again greatly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 迫洹水，悅軍走橋，橋已焚矣。

translations.literal: Pressed to the Huan River, Yue's army ran for the bridge; the bridge was already burned.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed to the Huan River, Yue's army ran for the bridge. The bridge was already burned.

sentences.zh: 悅軍亂，赴水，斬首二萬余級，殺大將孫晉卿、安墨啜，生獲三千余人，溺死者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Yue's army was in chaos and rushed into the water; more than twenty thousand heads were cut off, great generals Sun Jinqing and An Mochuo were killed, more than three thousand were captured alive, and the drowned dead were past counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's army was in chaos and rushed into the water. More than twenty thousand heads were cut off, great generals Sun Jinqing and An Mochuo were killed, more than three thousand were captured alive, and the drowned dead were past counting.

sentences.zh: 淄青軍殆盡，死者相枕藉三十餘里。

translations.literal: The Ziqing army was nearly wiped out; the dead lay piled for more than thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: The Ziqing army was nearly wiped out. The dead lay piled for more than thirty li.

sentences.zh: 悅收敗卒千余人走魏州，至門，州將李長春閉門不納。

translations.literal: Yue gathered more than a thousand defeated troops and fled to Wei Prefecture; at the gate the prefectural commander Li Changchun closed the gate and would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue gathered more than a thousand defeated troops and fled to Wei Prefecture. At the gate the prefectural commander Li Changchun closed the gate and would not admit him.

sentences.zh: 久之，追兵不至，比明，乃納悅。

translations.literal: After a long time pursuers did not arrive; near dawn he was admitted.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time pursuers did not arrive. Near dawn he was admitted.

sentences.zh: 悅既入，殺長春，嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Once Yue entered he killed Changchun and walled the city to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yue entered he killed Changchun and walled the city to hold it.

sentences.zh: 數日，李再春以博州降，悅兄昂以洺州降，王光進以長橋降。

translations.literal: After several days Li Zaichun surrendered Bo Prefecture, Yue's elder brother Ang surrendered Ming Prefecture, and Wang Guangjin surrendered Changqiao.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Li Zaichun surrendered Bo Prefecture, Yue's elder brother Ang surrendered Ming Prefecture, and Wang Guangjin surrendered Changqiao.

sentences.zh: 悅遣符璘、李瑤將五百騎送淄青兵還鎮，璘、瑤因來降燧。

translations.literal: Yue sent Fu Lin and Li Yao with five hundred horsemen to escort Ziqing troops back to garrison; Lin and Yao then came to surrender to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yue sent Fu Lin and Li Yao with five hundred horsemen to escort Ziqing troops back to garrison. Lin and Yao then came to surrender to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 魏州先引御河入城南流，燧令塞其領口，河流絕，城中益恐。

translations.literal: Wei Prefecture had earlier led the Imperial Canal into the city flowing south; Sui ordered the mouth blocked, the river flow cut off, and fear in the city increased.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Prefecture had earlier led the Imperial Canal into the city flowing south. Ma Sui ordered the mouth blocked, the river flow cut off, and fear in the city increased.

sentences.zh: 悅乃遣許士則、侯臧徒步間行說硃滔、王武俊，借兵求救。

translations.literal: Yue then sent Xu Shize and Hou Zang on foot by hidden routes to persuade Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun to borrow troops for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then sent Xu Shize and Hou Zang on foot by hidden routes to persuade Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun to borrow troops for rescue.

sentences.zh: 時王武俊已殺李惟嶽，傳首京師，授武俊恆冀觀察都防禦使；

translations.literal: At that time Wang Wujun had already killed Li Weiyue and sent his head to the capital and was appointed Hengji observation and defense commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Wujun had already killed Li Weiyue and sent his head to the capital and was appointed Hengji observation and defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時武俊同列張孝忠已為易定節度使，武俊獨為防禦使，又割趙、深二州為一鎮，以康日知為觀察使，甚為怨望，且素輕孝忠，恥名在下。

translations.literal: Wujun's colleague Zhang Xiaozhong had already become Yiding military commissioner; Wujun alone was defense commissioner, and Zhao and Shen prefectures were cut off as one command with Kang Rizhi as observation commissioner—he was deeply resentful and had always looked down on Xiaozhong, ashamed that his title ranked below.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun's colleague Zhang Xiaozhong had already become Yiding military commissioner. Wujun alone was defense commissioner, and Zhao and Shen prefectures were cut off as one command with Kang Rizhi as observation commissioner—he was deeply resentful and had always looked down on Xiaozhong, ashamed that his title ranked below.

sentences.zh: 時硃滔討李惟嶽，拔深州，求隸幽州不得，亦怨望。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Tao was attacking Li Weiyue, took Shen Prefecture, and asked to be subordinated to You Prefecture but was not granted it—he too was resentful.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Tao was attacking Li Weiyue, took Shen Prefecture, and asked to be subordinated to You Prefecture but was not granted it—he too was resentful.

sentences.zh: 由是滔、武俊同謀救悅。

translations.literal: Thus Tao and Wujun conspired together to rescue Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun conspired together to rescue Yue.

sentences.zh: 悅恃燕、趙之援，又出兵二萬背城而陣，燧復與諸軍擊破之。

translations.literal: Yue relied on aid from Yan and Zhao and again sent out twenty thousand troops to array with their backs to the city; Sui again joined the armies and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue relied on aid from Yan and Zhao and again sent out twenty thousand troops to array with their backs to the city. Ma Sui again joined the armies and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 五月，加燧同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Sui was promoted concurrent Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ma Sui was promoted concurrent Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 六月，硃滔、王武俊聯兵五萬來救悅，至於城下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun joined armies of fifty thousand to rescue Yue and reached below the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun joined armies of fifty thousand to rescue Yue and reached below the city.

sentences.zh: 諸帥議退兵，燧固不可，德宗遣朔方節度使李懷光將朔方軍步騎萬五千人赴燧。

translations.literal: The commanders discussed withdrawing troops; Sui firmly refused; Dezong sent Shuofang military commissioner Li Huai'guang with fifteen thousand Shuofang foot and horse to go to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders discussed withdrawing troops. Ma Sui firmly refused. Emperor Dezong sent Shuofang military commissioner Li Huai'guang with fifteen thousand Shuofang foot and horse to go to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 是月晦，懷光亦至。

translations.literal: On the last day of that month Huai'guang also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of that month Li Huai'guang also arrived.

sentences.zh: 懷光勇而無謀，軍至之日，未休息，堅請與滔等戰，王師不利。

translations.literal: Huai'guang was brave but without stratagem; the day the army arrived, without rest he firmly asked to fight Tao and the others, and the imperial army was unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang was brave but without stratagem. The day the army arrived, without rest he firmly asked to fight Zhu Tao and the others, and the imperial army was unfavorable.

sentences.zh: 悅等決水灌燧等軍，燧兵屈糧少，七月，燧與諸軍退次魏縣。

translations.literal: Yue and the others released water to flood Sui's army and others; Sui's troops were bent and grain was scarce; in the seventh month Sui and the armies withdrew and halted at Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and the others released water to flood Ma Sui's army and others. Sui's troops were bent and grain was scarce. In the seventh month Ma Sui and the armies withdrew and halted at Wei County.

sentences.zh: 是月，詔加燧魏州大都督府長史，兼魏、博、貝四州節度、觀察、招討等使。

translations.literal: That month an edict promoted Sui chief administrator of the Wei Prefecture metropolitan prefecture, concurrently military commissioner, observer, and pacification commissioner of Wei, Bo, and Bei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: That month an edict promoted Ma Sui chief administrator of the Wei Prefecture metropolitan prefecture, concurrently military commissioner, observer, and pacification commissioner of Wei, Bo, and Bei prefectures.

sentences.zh: 田悅、硃滔、王武俊軍亦至魏縣，與官軍隔河對壘。

translations.literal: Tian Yue, Zhu Tao, and Wang Wujun's armies also reached Wei County and faced the imperial army across the river in opposing camps.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue, Zhu Tao, and Wang Wujun's armies also reached Wei County and faced the imperial army across the river in opposing camps.

sentences.zh: 十一月，三盜於魏縣軍中遞相推獎王號：硃滔稱冀王，田悅稱魏王，王武俊稱趙王；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the three bandits in the Wei County army in turn praised one another's royal titles: Tao called himself King of Ji, Yue King of Wei, Wujun King of Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the three bandits in the Wei County army in turn praised one another's royal titles: Zhu Tao called himself King of Ji, Tian Yue King of Wei, Wang Wujun King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 又遣使於李納，納稱齊王。

translations.literal: they again sent envoys to Li Na, and Na called himself King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: They again sent envoys to Li Na, and Na called himself King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 四道共推淮西李希烈為天下兵馬元帥、太尉、建興王，皆偽署官號，如國初行臺之制，而名目頗有妖僻者，然未敢偽稱年號。

translations.literal: The four routes together promoted Huai Prefecture Li Xilie as grand marshal of all armies under Heaven, Grand Commandant, and King of Jianxing—all falsely appointing office titles like the founding era's mobile-court system, yet the names were somewhat strange and perverse, and they still did not dare falsely proclaim reign titles.
translations.idiomatic: The four routes together promoted Huai Prefecture Li Xilie as grand marshal of all armies under Heaven, Grand Commandant, and King of Jianxing—all falsely appointing office titles like the founding era's mobile-court system, yet the names were somewhat strange and perverse, and they still did not dare falsely proclaim reign titles.

sentences.zh: 而五盜合從圖傾社稷，兩河鼎沸，寇盜橫行；

translations.literal: The five bandits allied to overturn the state; the two rivers boiled; bandits and robbers ran wild;
translations.idiomatic: The five bandits allied to overturn the state. The two rivers boiled. Bandits and robbers ran wild.

sentences.zh: 燧等雖誌在勤王，竟莫能驅攘患難。

translations.literal: though Sui and others were intent on aiding the throne, in the end they could not drive off and scatter the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ma Sui and others were intent on aiding the throne, in the end they could not drive off and scatter the calamity.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，涇師犯關，帝幸奉天，燧引軍還太原。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year the Jing troops violated the capital; the emperor went to Fengtian, and Sui led his army back to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year the Jing troops violated the capital. The emperor went to Fengtian, and Ma Sui led his army back to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 議者云：「燧若乘田悅洹水之敗，並力攻之，時城中敗卒無三二千人，皆夷傷未起，日夕俟降；

translations.literal: Commentators said: "If Sui had taken Tian Yue's defeat at the Huan River and joined strength to attack, at that time defeated troops in the city were no more than two or three thousand, all wounded and not yet risen, waiting morning and evening to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said, "If Ma Sui had taken Tian Yue's defeat at the Huan River and joined strength to attack, at that time defeated troops in the city were no more than two or three thousand, all wounded and not yet risen, waiting morning and evening to surrender.

sentences.zh: 燧與抱真不和，遷延於擊賊，乃致三盜連結，至今為梗，職燧之由。」

translations.literal: Sui and Baozhen were not harmonious and delayed striking the bandits, thus causing the three bandits to link up—still an obstruction to this day—the fault lies with Sui."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui and Li Baozhen were not harmonious and delayed striking the bandits, thus causing the three bandits to link up—still an obstruction to this day—the fault lies with Ma Sui."

sentences.zh: 燧至太原，遣行軍司馬王權將兵五千赴奉天，又遣男匯及大將之子與俱來，壁於中渭橋。

translations.literal: When Sui reached Taiyuan he sent mobile-camp marshal Wang Quan with five thousand troops to go to Fengtian, and also sent his son Hui and great generals' sons to come together, walling at Zhongwei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Sui reached Taiyuan he sent mobile-camp marshal Wang Quan with five thousand troops to go to Fengtian, and also sent his son Hui and great generals' sons to come together, walling at Zhongwei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 及帝幸梁州，權、匯領兵還鎮。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Liang Prefecture, Quan and Hui led troops back to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Liang Prefecture, Wang Quan and Hui led troops back to garrison.

sentences.zh: 燧以晉陽王業所起，度都城東面平易受敵，時天下騷動，北邊數有警急，乃引晉水架汾而註城之東，瀦以為池，寇至計省守陴者萬人；

translations.literal: Sui, because Jinyang was where the Jin kings' enterprise rose, judged the eastern side of the capital level and easy to receive attack; at that time the empire was in turmoil and the northern frontier repeatedly had urgent alarms; he then led the Jin River over the Fen on trestles to pour east of the city, dammed it to make pools, and when bandits came reckoned ten thousand fewer needed to man the walls;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui, because Jinyang was where the Jin kings' enterprise rose, judged the eastern side of the capital level and easy to receive attack. At that time the empire was in turmoil and the northern frontier repeatedly had urgent alarms. He then led the Jin River over the Fen on trestles to pour east of the city, dammed it to make pools, and when bandits came reckoned ten thousand fewer needed to man the walls.

sentences.zh: 又決汾水環城，多為池沼，樹柳以固堤。

translations.literal: he again cut the Fen River to ring the city, made many pools and marshes, and planted willows to strengthen the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: He again cut the Fen River to ring the city, made many pools and marshes, and planted willows to strengthen the dikes.

sentences.zh: 尋兼保寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he also held the Baoning Army military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also held the Baoning Army military commission.

sentences.zh: 興元元年正月，加檢校司徒，封北平郡王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xingyuan he was promoted acting Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Xingyuan he was promoted acting Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 七月，德宗還京，加燧奉誠軍及晉、絳、慈、隰節度並管內諸軍行營副元帥，令與侍中渾瑊、鎮國軍節度使駱元光同討河中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Dezong returned to the capital and promoted Sui Fengcheng Army and Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi military commissions and deputy grand marshal of all armies within the circuit's mobile camp, ordering him with Palace Attendant Hun Jian and Zhenguo Army military commissioner Luo Yuanguang jointly to attack Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Emperor Dezong returned to the capital and promoted Ma Sui Fengcheng Army and Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi military commissions and deputy grand marshal of all armies within the circuit's mobile camp, ordering him with Palace Attendant Hun Jian and Zhenguo Army military commissioner Luo Yuanguang jointly to attack Hedong.

sentences.zh: 初，李懷光據河中，燧遣使招諭之，懷光妹婿要廷珍守晉州，衙將毛朝敭守隰州，鄭抗守慈州，皆相次降燧。

translations.literal: At first Li Huai'guang held Hedong; Sui sent envoys to summon and instruct him; Huai'guang's brother-in-law Yao Tingzhen held Jin Prefecture, yamen general Mao Chaoyi held Xi Prefecture, and Zheng Kang held Ci Prefecture—all in succession surrendered to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Huai'guang held Hedong. Ma Sui sent envoys to summon and instruct him. Huai'guang's brother-in-law Yao Tingzhen held Jin Prefecture, yamen general Mao Chaoyi held Xi Prefecture, and Zheng Kang held Ci Prefecture—all in succession surrendered to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 初，王武俊自魏縣還鎮，雖去偽號，而攻圍趙州不解，康日知窘蹙，欲棄趙州，燧奏曰：「可詔武俊與抱真同擊硃滔，以深、趙隸武俊，請改日知為晉、慈、隰節度使。」

translations.literal: At first Wang Wujun returned to garrison from Wei County; though he removed false titles he did not lift the siege of Zhao Prefecture; Kang Rizhi was in distress and wished to abandon Zhao Prefecture; Sui memorialized: "One may edict Wujun and Baozhen jointly to attack Zhu Tao, subordinate Shen and Zhao to Wujun, and request changing Rizhi to Jin, Ci, and Xi military commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: At first Wang Wujun returned to garrison from Wei County. Though he removed false titles he did not lift the siege of Zhao Prefecture. Kang Rizhi was in distress and wished to abandon Zhao Prefecture. Ma Sui memorialized, "One may edict Wujun and Baozhen jointly to attack Zhu Tao, subordinate Shen and Zhao to Wujun, and request changing Rizhi to Jin, Ci, and Xi military commissioner."

sentences.zh: 日知未至而三州降燧，故又加燧晉、慈、隰節度使。

translations.literal: Rizhi had not yet arrived when the three prefectures surrendered to Sui; therefore Sui was again made Jin, Ci, and Xi military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi had not yet arrived when the three prefectures surrendered to Ma Sui. Therefore Ma Sui was again made Jin, Ci, and Xi military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 燧乃表讓三州於日知，且言因降而授之，恐後有功者踵以為常。

translations.literal: Sui then memorialized yielding the three prefectures to Rizhi and said that because they surrendered and were granted them, he feared later men of merit would follow this as custom.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then memorialized yielding the three prefectures to Rizhi and said that because they surrendered and were granted them, he feared later men of merit would follow this as custom.

sentences.zh: 上嘉而許之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this and granted it.

sentences.zh: 燧乃遣使迎日知，既至，籍府庫而歸之，日知喜且過望。

translations.literal: Sui then sent envoys to welcome Rizhi; once he arrived he registered the treasury stores and returned them; Rizhi was pleased beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then sent envoys to welcome Rizhi. Once he arrived he registered the treasury stores and returned them. Rizhi was pleased beyond expectation.

sentences.zh: 九月十五日，燧帥步騎三萬次於絳，分兵收夏縣，略稷山，攻龍門，降其將馮萬興、任象玉。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month Sui led thirty thousand foot and horse and halted at Jiang, divided troops to take Xia County, raided Jishan, attacked Longmen, and reduced its generals Feng Wanxing and Ren Xiangyu.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month Ma Sui led thirty thousand foot and horse and halted at Jiang, divided troops to take Xia County, raided Jishan, attacked Longmen, and reduced its generals Feng Wanxing and Ren Xiangyu.

sentences.zh: 燧以兵攻絳州，十月，拔其外城，其夜偽刺史王克同與大將達奚小進棄城走，降其眾四千人。

translations.literal: Sui with troops attacked Jiang Prefecture; in the tenth month they took the outer city; that night false prefect Wang Ketong with great general Daxi Xiaojin abandoned the city and fled, reducing its masses of four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui with troops attacked Jiang Prefecture. In the tenth month they took the outer city. That night false prefect Wang Ketong with great general Daxi Xiaojin abandoned the city and fled, reducing its masses of four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 又遣大將李自良、谷秀分兵略定聞喜、夏縣、萬泉、虞鄉、永樂、猗氏六縣，降其將辛兟及兵五千人。

translations.literal: He again sent great generals Li Ziliang and Gu Xiu to divide troops and pacify Wenxi, Xia County, Wanquan, Yuxiang, Yongle, and Yishi six counties, reducing their general Xin Shen and five thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent great generals Li Ziliang and Gu Xiu to divide troops and pacify Wenxi, Xia County, Wanquan, Yuxiang, Yongle, and Yishi six counties, reducing their general Xin Shen and five thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 谷秀以犯令虜士女，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Gu Xiu because he violated orders and plundered soldiers' women was beheaded to announce to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xiu because he violated orders and plundered soldiers' women was beheaded to announce to the army.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，軍次寶鼎，敗賊騎兵於陶城，前鋒將李黯追擊之，射殺賊將徐伯文，斬首萬餘級，獲馬五百匹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan the army halted at Baoding and defeated bandit cavalry at Taocheng; vanguard general Li An pursued them, shot and killed bandit general Xu Bowen, cut off more than ten thousand heads, and captured five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan the army halted at Baoding and defeated bandit cavalry at Taocheng. Vanguard general Li An pursued them, shot and killed bandit general Xu Bowen, cut off more than ten thousand heads, and captured five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下蝗旱，物價騰踴，軍乏糧餉，而京師言事多請捨懷光，上意未決。

translations.literal: That year locusts and drought afflicted all under Heaven, prices soared, the army lacked grain supplies, and at the capital memorialists mostly asked to pardon Huai'guang; the emperor's mind was not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: That year locusts and drought afflicted all under Heaven, prices soared, the army lacked grain supplies, and at the capital memorialists mostly asked to pardon Li Huai'guang. The emperor's mind was not yet decided.

sentences.zh: 燧以懷光逆節尤甚，河中密邇京邑，反覆不可保信，舍之無以示天下，慮上為左右所惑，且兵事尚密。

translations.literal: Sui, because Huai'guang's rebellious conduct was especially grave and Hedong lay close to the capital, treacherous and unreliable, to pardon him would show nothing to all under Heaven; he feared the emperor would be misled by those around him, and military matters should still be secret.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui, because Huai'guang's rebellious conduct was especially grave and Hedong lay close to the capital, treacherous and unreliable—to pardon him would show nothing to all under Heaven. He feared the emperor would be misled by those around him, and military matters should still be secret.

sentences.zh: 六月，燧乃舍軍以數百騎朝於京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Sui then left the army with several hundred horsemen to attend court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Ma Sui then left the army with several hundred horsemen to attend court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 比召見，燧曰：「臣雖不武，得芻糧支一月，足以平河中。」

translations.literal: When summoned to audience Sui said: "Your subject though not martial, with fodder and grain for one month is enough to pacify Hedong."
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to audience Ma Sui said, "Your subject though not martial, with fodder and grain for one month is enough to pacify Hedong."

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 七月，燧因朝京師，乃與渾瑊、駱元光、韓遊瑰合軍，次於長春宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, because Sui attended court at the capital, he joined Hun Jian, Luo Yuanguang, and Han Yougui in armies and halted at Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, because Ma Sui attended court at the capital, he joined Hun Jian, Luo Yuanguang, and Han Yougui in armies and halted at Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 懷光將徐廷光以兵六千守宮城，禦備甚嚴。

translations.literal: Huai'guang's general Xu Tingguang with six thousand troops held the palace city; defenses were very strict.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang's general Xu Tingguang with six thousand troops held the palace city. Defenses were very strict.

sentences.zh: 燧度長春不下，則懷光自固，攻之曠日持久，所傷必甚，乃挺身至城下呼廷光。

translations.literal: Sui judged that if Changchun could not be taken Huai'guang would hold firm; attacking would take long days and casualties must be heavy; he then went in person to below the city and called Tingguang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui judged that if Changchun could not be taken Huai'guang would hold firm. Attacking would take long days and casualties must be heavy. He then went in person to below the city and called Xu Tingguang.

sentences.zh: 廷光素憚燧威名，則拜於城上。

translations.literal: Tingguang had always feared Sui's martial name and bowed on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tingguang had always feared Ma Sui's martial name and bowed on the wall.

sentences.zh: 燧度廷光心已屈，乃徐謂之曰：「我來自朝廷，可西面受命。」

translations.literal: Sui judged Tingguang's heart already bent and slowly said to him: "I come from the court; you may face west to receive orders."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui judged Xu Tingguang's heart already bent and slowly said to him, "I come from the court. You may face west to receive orders."

sentences.zh: 廷光復拜。

translations.literal: Tingguang bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tingguang bowed again.

sentences.zh: 燧乃喻之曰：「公等皆朔方將士，祿山以來，首建大動，四十餘年，功伐最高，奈何棄祖父之動力，背君上，為族滅之計耶！

translations.literal: Sui then instructed him: "You all are Shuofang soldiers; since Lushu, foremost in great merit, more than forty years, merit in battle highest—why abandon your grandfathers' merit, turn against your sovereign, and take the plan of clan extinction!
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui then instructed him, "You all are Shuofang soldiers. Since Lushu, foremost in great merit, more than forty years, merit in battle highest—why abandon your grandfathers' merit, turn against your sovereign, and take the plan of clan extinction?

sentences.zh: 從吾，非止免禍，富貴可圖也。」

translations.literal: Follow me—not only escape calamity; wealth and honor can be plotted."
translations.idiomatic: Follow me—not only escape calamity. Wealth and honor can be plotted."

sentences.zh: 賊徒皆不對。

translations.literal: The bandit masses all did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit masses all did not answer.

sentences.zh: 燧又曰：「爾以吾言不誠，今相去不遠數步，爾當射我！」

translations.literal: Sui again said: "You think my words not sincere—now we are not far apart by several paces; you ought to shoot me!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui again said, "You think my words not sincere—now we are not far apart by several paces. You ought to shoot me!"

sentences.zh: 乃披襟示之。

translations.literal: He then bared his breast to show them.
translations.idiomatic: He then bared his breast to show them.

sentences.zh: 廷光感泣俯伏，軍士亦泣下。

translations.literal: Tingguang wept and prostrated himself; the soldiers also wept.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tingguang wept and prostrated himself. The soldiers also wept.

sentences.zh: 先一日，賊焦籬堡守將尉珪以兵二千因堡降燧；

translations.literal: One day earlier the bandit Jiaoli Fort garrison commander Wei Gui with two thousand troops because of the fort surrendered to Sui;
translations.idiomatic: One day earlier the bandit Jiaoli Fort garrison commander Wei Gui with two thousand troops because of the fort surrendered to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 廷光東道既絕，乃率眾出降。

translations.literal: Tingguang's eastern route was already cut and he then led the masses out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tingguang's eastern route was already cut and he then led the masses out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 燧以數騎徑入城，處之不疑，莫不畏服，眾大呼曰：「吾輩復得為王人矣！」

translations.literal: Sui with several horsemen went straight into the city and treated them without suspicion; all feared and submitted; the masses greatly shouted: "We again can be the king's men!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui with several horsemen went straight into the city and treated them without suspicion. All feared and submitted. The masses greatly shouted, "We again can be the king's men!"

sentences.zh: 渾瑊由是服燧，私謂參佐曰：「予嘗謂馬公用兵與予不相遠，但警怪累敗田悅；

translations.literal: Hun Jian from this submitted to Sui and privately told his staff: "I once said Duke Ma's use of troops was not far from mine, but was only startled and wondered at repeatedly defeating Tian Yue;
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian from this submitted to Ma Sui and privately told his staff, "I once said Duke Ma's use of troops was not far from mine, but was only startled and wondered at repeatedly defeating Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 今觀其行兵料敵，吾不迨遠矣！」

translations.literal: now seeing him march troops and measure the enemy, I do not reach far!"
translations.idiomatic: Now seeing him march troops and measure the enemy, I do not reach far!"

sentences.zh: 八月，燧移軍於焦籬堡。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Sui moved the army to Jiaoli Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Ma Sui moved the army to Jiaoli Fort.

sentences.zh: 其夜，賊太原堡守將吳冏棄堡而遁，其下皆降。

translations.literal: That night the bandit Taiyuan Fort garrison commander Wu Jiong abandoned the fort and fled; those below all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: That night the bandit Taiyuan Fort garrison commander Wu Jiong abandoned the fort and fled. Those below all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 燧率諸軍濟河，兵凡八萬，陣於城下。

translations.literal: Sui led the armies across the river; troops totaled eighty thousand and arrayed below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui led the armies across the river. Troops totaled eighty thousand and arrayed below the city.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊將牛名俊斬懷光首以城降。

translations.literal: That day bandit general Niu Mingjun beheaded Huai'guang's head and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: That day bandit general Niu Mingjun beheaded Li Huai'guang's head and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 其守兵猶一萬六千人，斬賊將閻晏、孟寶、張清、吳冏等七人以徇，為懷光脅虜者皆舍之。

translations.literal: Its garrison still had sixteen thousand men; bandit generals Yan Yan, Meng Bao, Zhang Qing, Wu Jiong and seven others were beheaded to announce to the army; those coerced and captured by Huai'guang were all released.
translations.idiomatic: Its garrison still had sixteen thousand men. Bandit generals Yan Yan, Meng Bao, Zhang Qing, Wu Jiong and seven others were beheaded to announce to the army. Those coerced and captured by Huai'guang were all released.

sentences.zh: 燧自朝京師還行營，凡二十七日而河中平。

translations.literal: From Sui's return to court to the mobile camp was twenty-seven days in all and Hedong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: From Ma Sui's return to court to the mobile camp was twenty-seven days in all and Hedong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔書褒美，遷光祿大夫，兼侍中，仍與一子五品正員官。

translations.literal: An edict praised and commended him; he was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and concurrently Palace Attendant, and one son was given a fifth-rank regular office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised and commended him. He was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and concurrently Palace Attendant, and one son was given a fifth-rank regular office.

sentences.zh: 宴賜畢，還太原。

translations.literal: When the feast and gifts were finished he returned to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast and gifts were finished he returned to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 是行也，德宗賜燧《宸扆》、《臺衡》二銘。

translations.literal: On this journey Dezong gave Sui the two inscriptions Chenyi and Taiheng.
translations.idiomatic: On this journey Emperor Dezong gave Ma Sui the two inscriptions Chenyi and Taiheng.

sentences.zh: 序曰：

translations.literal: The preface says:
translations.idiomatic: The preface says:

sentences.zh: 《宸扆銘》曰：

translations.literal: The Chenyi Inscription says:
translations.idiomatic: The Chenyi Inscription says:

sentences.zh: 天生蒸人，性命元淳，嗜欲交馳，利害糾紛。

translations.literal: Heaven bore the teeming people; life and nature are originally pure; desire and profit rush together; benefit and harm tangle in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven bore the teeming people. Life and nature are originally pure. Desire and profit rush together; benefit and harm tangle in confusion.

sentences.zh: 無主乃亂，樹之以君，九域茫茫，萬情云云。

translations.literal: Without a lord there is chaos; establish a lord to govern them; the nine regions vast and dim; ten thousand feelings cloud upon cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Without a lord there is chaos. Establish a lord to govern them. The nine regions are vast and dim; ten thousand feelings cloud upon cloud.

sentences.zh: 目不備睹，耳難遍聞，睹之聞之，矧又非真。

translations.literal: The eye cannot prepare to see all; the ear cannot hear everywhere; what is seen and heard—moreover is not true.
translations.idiomatic: The eye cannot prepare to see all. The ear cannot hear everywhere. What is seen and heard—moreover is not true.

sentences.zh: 事失其源，道遠莫親，理行其要，化行如神。

translations.literal: Affairs lose their source; the Way is far and kinship hard; principle holds to essentials; transforming conduct is like spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs lose their source. The Way is far and kinship hard. Principle holds to essentials; transforming conduct is like spirit.

sentences.zh: 失源維何，不自正身，正身之方，先誠其意。

translations.literal: What loses the source—how? Not correcting oneself first; the method of correcting oneself—first make sincere the intent.
translations.idiomatic: What loses the source? Not correcting oneself first. The method of correcting oneself is first to make sincere the intent.

sentences.zh: 罔從爾欲，罔載爾偽，體道崇德，本仁率義。

translations.literal: Do not follow your desires; do not carry your falsity; embody the Way, honor virtue, root in benevolence, lead in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Do not follow your desires. Do not carry your falsity. Embody the Way, honor virtue, root in benevolence, lead in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 必信若寒暑，無私象天地，感而遂通，百慮一致。

translations.literal: Trust must be like cold and heat; without partiality like Heaven and earth; moved then it passes through; a hundred thoughts become one.
translations.idiomatic: Trust must be like cold and heat. Without partiality like Heaven and earth. Moved, then it passes through; a hundred thoughts become one.

sentences.zh: 任人之術，各當其器，舍短從長，理無求備。

translations.literal: The method of employing men—each suited to his instrument; abandon the short, follow the long; in principle do not seek completeness.
translations.idiomatic: The method of employing men is to suit each to his instrument. Abandon the short, follow the long. In principle do not seek completeness.

sentences.zh: 事多總集，眾才鹹遂，知而必任，任而勿貳。

translations.literal: Affairs mostly gather in the whole; the talents of the masses all succeed; know and then surely employ; employ and do not be of two minds.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs mostly gather in the whole. The talents of the masses all succeed. Know and then surely employ. Employ and do not be of two minds.

sentences.zh: 以天下之目為鑒，我鑒斯明；

translations.literal: Take all under Heaven's eyes as mirror—my mirror then is bright;
translations.idiomatic: Take all under Heaven's eyes as mirror—my mirror then is bright.

sentences.zh: 以天下之心為謀，我謀則智。

translations.literal: take all under Heaven's hearts as counsel—my counsel then is wise.
translations.idiomatic: Take all under Heaven's hearts as counsel—my counsel then is wise.

sentences.zh: 求賢惟廣，辯理惟精，逆耳咈心，必嘉乃誠。

translations.literal: Seek the worthy as broadly as possible; distinguish principle as finely as possible; words that jar the ear and offend the heart—you must prize their sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Seek the worthy as broadly as possible. Distinguish principle as finely as possible. Words that jar the ear and offend the heart—you must prize their sincerity.

sentences.zh: 順旨茍容，亦察其情，斥去奸諛，全度忠貞。

translations.literal: Words that accord with intent and tolerate appearance—you must also examine their feeling; drive away flatterers and sycophants; fully measure loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Words that accord with intent and tolerate appearance—you must also examine their feeling. Drive away flatterers and sycophants. Fully measure loyalty and uprightness.

sentences.zh: 先人立言，為代作程，諤諤者昌，唯唯者傾，系以興亡，曷雲其輕。

translations.literal: Those before us established words as models for the age; blunt speech brings prosperity, mere assent brings ruin; tied to rise and fall—how can it be called light?
translations.idiomatic: Those before us established words as models for the age. Blunt speech brings prosperity, mere assent brings ruin. Tied to rise and fall—how can it be called light?

sentences.zh: 承天子人，夫豈不貴？

translations.literal: Receiving Heaven's person as lord—is it not honored?
translations.idiomatic: Receiving Heaven's person as lord—is it not honored?

sentences.zh: 伊昔哲王，夙夜祗畏。

translations.literal: In ancient times the wise kings from dawn to dusk held awe.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times the wise kings from dawn to dusk held awe.

sentences.zh: 馭朽為戒，納隍為誌，神將害盈，天匪假易。

translations.literal: Take rotting wood as warning; take falling into the moat as resolve; the spirits will harm fullness; Heaven does not lend ease.
translations.idiomatic: Take rotting wood as warning. Take falling into the moat as resolve. The spirits will harm fullness. Heaven does not lend ease.

sentences.zh: 四海為家，夫豈不富？

translations.literal: The four seas as home—is it not rich?
translations.idiomatic: The four seas as home—is it not rich?

sentences.zh: 伊昔哲王，勤儉固陋。

translations.literal: In ancient times the wise kings were diligent and thrifty, firmly plain.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times the wise kings were diligent and thrifty, firmly plain.

sentences.zh: 土階罔飾，露臺罷構，遠奇伎淫巧，放珍禽怪獸。

translations.literal: Earthen steps unadorned; the dew platform ceased to be built; keep far from strange skills and licentious craft; release rare birds and monstrous beasts.
