translations.idiomatic: Earthen steps unadorned. The dew platform ceased to be built. Keep far from strange skills and licentious craft. Release rare birds and monstrous beasts.

sentences.zh: 敬之慎之，天命可祐。

translations.literal: Revere it, be careful of it—Heaven's mandate can be aided.
translations.idiomatic: Revere it, be careful of it—Heaven's mandate can be aided.

sentences.zh: 欲令必行，順人之情，欲誠必著，清己之慮，心無億詐，事必忠恕。

translations.literal: To make orders surely carried out—accord with men's feelings; to make sincerity surely shown—clear one's own concerns; heart without deceit; affairs must be loyal and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: To make orders surely carried out, accord with men's feelings. To make sincerity surely shown, clear one's own concerns. Heart without deceit. Affairs must be loyal and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 凡將有為，靡不三思，喜怒以節，動靜以時。

translations.literal: Whatever a lord will do—none without thrice thinking; joy and anger by measure; movement and stillness by season.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever a lord will do—none without thrice thinking. Joy and anger by measure. Movement and stillness by season.

sentences.zh: 毫厘或差，禍害亦隨，慢易厥初，悔其曷追。

translations.literal: A hair's breadth off—or calamity follows; treating the beginning lightly—how can one regret and pursue?
translations.idiomatic: A hair's breadth off—or calamity follows. Treating the beginning lightly—how can one regret and pursue?

sentences.zh: 刑不可長，武不可恃，作威逞力，厲階斯起。

translations.literal: Punishment cannot be prolonged; martial power cannot be relied on; making awe, displaying force—the steps of calamity rise from this.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment cannot be prolonged. Martial power cannot be relied on. Making awe, displaying force—the steps of calamity rise from this.

sentences.zh: 垂旒蔽聰，黈纊塞耳，含弘光大，是亦為美。

translations.literal: The hanging tassels screen hearing; the yellow cap blocks the ear; containing and magnifying the bright—that too is beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: The hanging tassels screen hearing. The yellow cap blocks the ear. Containing and magnifying the bright—that too is beautiful.

sentences.zh: 覆之如天，愛之如子，仁心感人，率土自理。

translations.literal: Covering like Heaven; loving like a child; benevolent heart moves men; all the land governs itself.
translations.idiomatic: Covering like Heaven. Loving like a child. Benevolent heart moves men. All the land governs itself.

sentences.zh: 嗟予寡昧，嗣守丕圖，寇戎薦興，德化未孚。

translations.literal: Alas my few and dim; I inherit and keep the great plan; bandits and barbarians repeatedly rise; virtue and transforming have not yet reached.
translations.idiomatic: Alas my few and dim. I inherit and keep the great plan. Bandits and barbarians repeatedly rise. Virtue and transforming have not yet reached.

sentences.zh: 大業兢兢，其敢以渝，俯察物情，仰稽典謨，作誡斯言，置於坐隅。

translations.literal: The great enterprise tremblingly—how dare I alter it? Bowing to examine things' feelings; looking up to classic models; making this admonition—place it at the seat's corner.
translations.idiomatic: The great enterprise tremblingly—how dare I alter it? Bowing to examine things' feelings. Looking up to classic models. Making this admonition—place it at the seat's corner.

sentences.zh: 《臺衡銘》曰：

translations.literal: The Taiheng Inscription says:
translations.idiomatic: The Taiheng Inscription says:

sentences.zh: 天列臺星，垂象於人，聖人則天，亦建輔臣。

translations.literal: Heaven arrays the terrace stars; they hang as images for men; the sage models Heaven and also establishes assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven arrays the terrace stars. They hang as images for men. The sage models Heaven and also establishes assisting ministers.

sentences.zh: 以翼以弼，為衡為鈞，如耳目應心，如股肱連身，是則同體，孰雲非親？

translations.literal: To wing and to assist, to be balance and steelyard—like ears and eyes responding to the heart, like arms and thighs joined to the body—that is one body; who says not kin?
translations.idiomatic: To wing and to assist, to be balance and steelyard—like ears and eyes responding to the heart, like arms and thighs joined to the body—that is one body. Who says not kin?

sentences.zh: 陰陽相推，四序成歲，君臣相得，萬邦作乂。

translations.literal: Yin and yang push one another; the four seasons complete the year; lord and minister obtain one another; the myriad states are governed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang push one another. The four seasons complete the year. Lord and minister obtain one another. The myriad states are governed.

sentences.zh: 感同風雲，合若符契，以道匡救，盡規獻替，木必從繩，金其用礪。

translations.literal: Feeling responds like wind and cloud; joining like tally and seal; with the Way to correct and save; fully advising and remonstrating; wood must follow the line; metal must use the whetstone.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling responds like wind and cloud. Joining like tally and seal. With the Way to correct and save. Fully advising and remonstrating. Wood must follow the line. Metal must use the whetstone.

sentences.zh: 帝者之盛，時惟陶唐，乃聞疇咨，仄陋明揚。

translations.literal: When emperors flourish—then only Tao Tang; then one heard broad consultation; from low and narrow the bright were chosen.
translations.idiomatic: When emperors flourish—then only Yao of Tang. Then one heard broad consultation. From low and narrow the bright were chosen.

sentences.zh: 洎乎有虞，二八騰芳。

translations.literal: Down to You Yu—the Eight Worthies rose in fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Emperor Shun—the Eight Worthies rose in fragrance.

sentences.zh: 爰迨伊尹，相於成湯。

translations.literal: Then reaching Yi Yin—he assisted Cheng Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Then reaching Yi Yin—he assisted Cheng Tang.

sentences.zh: 載生姜牙，諒彼武王。

translations.literal: Then Jiang Ziya—he trusted that King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jiang Ziya—he trusted that King Wu.

sentences.zh: 道無不行，謀無不臧，君聖臣賢，運泰時康。

translations.literal: The Way all followed; no plan was not good; lord sage, minister worthy; fortune smooth, times peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: The Way all followed. No plan was not good. Lord sage, minister worthy. Fortune smooth, times peaceful.

sentences.zh: 漢高既興，蕭、曹亦彰。

translations.literal: When Han the High rose—Xiao and Cao also shone.
translations.idiomatic: When Han the High rose—Xiao and Cao also shone.

sentences.zh: 烈烈我祖，膺期而昌，剷滅群兇，砥平四方。

translations.literal: Brightly our ancestor—he received the season and flourished; he cut down the mass of villains; he leveled the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Brightly our ancestor—he received the season and flourished. He cut down the mass of villains. He leveled the four directions.

sentences.zh: 惟衛及英，啟辟封疆；

translations.literal: Wei and Ying both—opened and established territories;
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Ying both—opened and established territories.

sentences.zh: 曰房與杜，振理維綱；

translations.literal: Fang and Du—raised governance and held the net;
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Du—raised governance and held the net.

sentences.zh: 亦有魏徵，忠謇昂昂。

translations.literal: There was also Wei Zheng—loyal and upright, high and bright.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wei Zheng—loyal and upright, high and bright.

sentences.zh: 偉茲眾材，為棟為梁，蕩蕩巍巍，邦家有光。

translations.literal: Great these many talents—as ridgepole and beam; vast and lofty—the state and family have light.
translations.idiomatic: Great these many talents—as ridgepole and beam. Vast and lofty—the state and family have light.

sentences.zh: 是知道之廢興，系於時主，主之得失，資於臺輔。

translations.literal: Thus the Way's abandonment and rise depend on the age's lord; the lord's gain and loss rely on the terrace assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Way's abandonment and rise depend on the age's lord. The lord's gain and loss rely on the terrace assistants.

sentences.zh: 經之以文，緯之以武，出為方伯，入作申、甫，絕維載張，闕袞斯補。

translations.literal: Warp it with culture; woof it with martial; going out as regional lords; entering as Shen and Fu; when the net breaks, load it again; when the robe is lacking, thus mend it.
translations.idiomatic: Warp it with culture. Woof it with martial. Going out as regional lords. Entering as Shen and Fu. When the net breaks, load it again. When the robe is lacking, thus mend it.

sentences.zh: 惟德是倚，惟才是求，人不易知，德亦難周。

translations.literal: Only virtue is leaned on; only talent is sought; men are not easy to know; virtue is also hard to exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Only virtue is leaned on. Only talent is sought. Men are not easy to know. Virtue is also hard to exhaust.

sentences.zh: 傅說板築，夷吾射鉤，任之不疑，千載垂休，體於至公，何鄙何讎。

translations.literal: Fuyue was wall-building; Guan Zhong shot the hook; employ without doubt—a thousand ages leave beauty; embody utmost fairness—what base, what foe?
translations.idiomatic: Fuyue was wall-building. Guan Zhong shot the hook. Employ without doubt—a thousand ages leave beauty. Embody utmost fairness—what base, what foe?

sentences.zh: 追惟哲主，必賴良弼，矧予不德，暗於理術。

translations.literal: Looking back to the wise lords—they must rely on good assistants; how much more I without virtue—dark in principle and arts.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back to the wise lords—they must rely on good assistants. How much more I without virtue—dark in principle and arts.

sentences.zh: 師旅繁起，政刑多失，遘茲艱屯，夙夜祗栗。

translations.literal: Armies and brigades repeatedly rise; government and punishment much lost; meeting this hardship and peril—from dawn to dusk respectful and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Armies and brigades repeatedly rise. Government and punishment much lost. Meeting this hardship and peril—from dawn to dusk respectful and fearful.

sentences.zh: 翊我戴我，實惟勛賢，內熙庶績，外總十連，威武載揚，謀猷日宣。

translations.literal: They aid me, they bear me—truly these meritorious worthies; within brightening the many achievements; without summing the ten circuits; martial awe displayed; plans and counsels daily proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: They aid me, they bear me—truly these meritorious worthies. Within brightening the many achievements. Without summing the ten circuits. Martial awe displayed. Plans and counsels daily proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 長城壓境，巨艦濟川，同德同心，扶危持顛。

translations.literal: Great Wall pressing the border; great ships crossing the river; same virtue, same heart; supporting danger, holding up collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wall pressing the border. Great ships crossing the river. Same virtue, same heart. Supporting danger, holding up collapse.

sentences.zh: 予嘉爾誠，爾相予理，惟後失道，亦臣之恥。

translations.literal: I praise your sincerity; you assist my governance; when the lord loses the Way—it is also the minister's shame.
translations.idiomatic: I praise your sincerity. You assist my governance. When the lord loses the Way—it is also the minister's shame.

sentences.zh: 自昔格言，慎終如始，功藏鼎彜，道冠圖史。

translations.literal: From ancient admonitions—be careful at the end as at the start; merit stored in the cauldron inscription; the Way crowns histories and annals.
translations.idiomatic: From ancient admonitions—be careful at the end as at the start. Merit stored in the cauldron inscription. The Way crowns histories and annals.

sentences.zh: 無俾伊、傅，克專厥美，作鑒勒銘，永世是紀。

translations.literal: Do not let Yi and Fu monopolize their beauty; make this mirror and inscribe it—forever is it recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let Yi and Fu monopolize their beauty. Make this mirror and inscribe it—forever is it recorded.

sentences.zh: 燧至太原，乃勒二銘於起義堂西偏，帝為題額，其崇寵如此。

translations.literal: When Sui reached Taiyuan he then carved the two inscriptions on the west side of the Uprising Hall; the emperor himself wrote the title—such was the honor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Sui reached Taiyuan he then carved the two inscriptions on the west side of the Uprising Hall. The emperor himself wrote the title—such was the honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，吐蕃大將尚結贊陷鹽、夏二州，各留兵守之，結贊大軍屯於鳴沙，自冬及春，羊馬多死，糧餉不繼。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year the Tibetan great general Shang Jiezan took Yan and Xia prefectures and left troops to hold each; Jiezan's great army encamped at Mingsha; from winter to spring many sheep and horses died and grain supplies did not continue.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year the Tibetan great general Shang Jiezan took Yan and Xia prefectures and left troops to hold each. Jiezan's great army encamped at Mingsha. From winter to spring many sheep and horses died and grain supplies did not continue.

sentences.zh: 德宗以燧為綏、銀、麟勝招討使，令與華帥駱元光、邠帥韓遊瑰及鳳翔諸鎮之師會於河西進討。

translations.literal: Dezong made Sui pacification commissioner of Sui, Yin, Lin, and Sheng and ordered him with Hua commander Luo Yuanguang, Bin commander Han Yougui, and the forces of Fengxiang and other garrisons to meet west of the river and advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong made Ma Sui pacification commissioner of Sui, Yin, Lin, and Sheng and ordered him with Hua commander Luo Yuanguang, Bin commander Han Yougui, and the forces of Fengxiang and other garrisons to meet west of the river and advance to attack.

sentences.zh: 燧出師，次石州。

translations.literal: Sui went out with the army and halted at Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui went out with the army and halted at Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 結贊聞之懼，遣使請和，仍約盟會，上皆不許。

translations.literal: Jiezan heard this and feared; he sent envoys to ask peace and also arranged alliance meetings; the emperor all did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan heard this and feared. He sent envoys to ask peace and also arranged alliance meetings. The emperor all did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 又遣其大將論頰熱厚禮卑辭申情於燧請和，燧頻表論奏，上堅不許。

translations.literal: He again sent his great general Lun Bire with heavy gifts and humble words to express feeling to Sui asking peace; Sui repeatedly memorialized and reported; the emperor firmly did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent his great general Lun Bire with heavy gifts and humble words to express feeling to Ma Sui asking peace. Sui repeatedly memorialized and reported. The emperor firmly did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，燧軍還太原。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Sui's army returned to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Ma Sui's army returned to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 四月，燧與論頰熱俱入朝，燧盛言蕃情可保，請許其盟，上然之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Sui and Lun Bire both entered court; Sui greatly said Tibetan feeling could be trusted and asked to grant their alliance; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Ma Sui and Lun Bire both entered court. Sui greatly said Tibetan feeling could be trusted and asked to grant their alliance. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 燧既入朝，結贊遽自鳴沙還蕃。

translations.literal: Once Sui entered court Jiezan hastily from Mingsha returned to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ma Sui entered court Jiezan hastily from Mingsha returned to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 是歲閏五月十五日，侍中渾瑊與蕃相尚結贊盟於平涼，為蕃軍所劫，狼狽僅免，陷將吏六十余員，由燧之謬謀也，坐是奪兵權。

translations.literal: That year on the fifteenth day of the intercalary fifth month Palace Attendant Hun Jian allied with Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan at Pingliang and was robbed by Tibetan troops; in distress he barely escaped; more than sixty officers and clerks were trapped—because of Sui's mistaken plan; for this he lost military authority.
translations.idiomatic: That year on the fifteenth day of the intercalary fifth month Palace Attendant Hun Jian allied with Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan at Pingliang and was robbed by Tibetan troops. In distress he barely escaped. More than sixty officers and clerks were trapped—because of Ma Sui's mistaken plan. For this he lost military authority.

sentences.zh: 六月，以燧守司徒，兼侍中、北平王如故，仍賜妓樂，奉朝請而已。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Sui was made Grand Mentor, concurrently Palace Attendant, Prince of Beiping as before, and was given singing girls; he attended court by invitation only.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Ma Sui was made Grand Mentor, concurrently Palace Attendant, Prince of Beiping as before, and was given singing girls. He attended court by invitation only.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，燧與太尉李晟召見於延英殿，上嘉其有大勛力，皆圖形淩煙閣，列於元臣之次。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year Sui and Grand Commandant Li Sheng were summoned to audience in the Yanying Hall; the emperor praised their great merit and power; both were pictured in the Lingyan Pavilion, ranked among the founding ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year Ma Sui and Grand Commandant Li Sheng were summoned to audience in the Yanying Hall. The emperor praised their great merit and power. Both were pictured in the Lingyan Pavilion, ranked among the founding ministers.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，燧對於延英。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year Sui answered at the Yanying.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year Ma Sui answered at the Yanying.

sentences.zh: 初，上以燧足疾，不令朝謁；

translations.literal: At first because the emperor thought Sui had foot ailment he did not order court audience;
translations.idiomatic: At first because the emperor thought Ma Sui had foot ailment he did not order court audience.

sentences.zh: 是日，燧以冬首入朝，敕許不拜而坐。

translations.literal: That day Sui at the winter start entered court; an edict permitted not bowing but sitting.
translations.idiomatic: That day Ma Sui at the winter start entered court. An edict permitted not bowing but sitting.

sentences.zh: 時太尉晟初薨，帝謂燧曰：「常時卿與太尉晟同來，今獨見卿，不覺悲慟。」

translations.literal: At that time Grand Commandant Sheng had just died; the emperor said to Sui: "Usually you and Grand Commandant Sheng came together; now I see you alone and cannot help feeling grief."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Commandant Li Sheng had just died. The emperor said to Ma Sui, "Usually you and Grand Commandant Sheng came together. Now I see you alone and cannot help feeling grief."

sentences.zh: 上歔欷久之。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed long.

sentences.zh: 燧既退，足疾，仆於地，上親掖起之，送及於陛，燧頓首泣謝。

translations.literal: Once Sui withdrew his foot ailment caused him to fall to the ground; the emperor personally helped him up and escorted him to the steps; Sui prostrated himself weeping in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ma Sui withdrew his foot ailment caused him to fall to the ground. The emperor personally helped him up and escorted him to the steps. Sui prostrated himself weeping in thanks.

sentences.zh: 累上表乞骸，陳讓侍中，優詔不許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; he stated yielding the Palace Attendant; gracious edicts did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized begging to retire. He stated yielding the Palace Attendant. Gracious edicts did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 貞元十一年八月薨，時年七十。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eleventh year of Zhenyuan he died; at that time he was seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eleventh year of Zhenyuan he died. At that time he was seventy.

sentences.zh: 先是，司天頻奏熒惑太白犯太微上將，間一月而燧薨。

translations.literal: Before this the Directorate of Astronomy repeatedly reported Mars and Venus invading the Grand Pivot's upper general; within a month Sui died.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the Directorate of Astronomy repeatedly reported Mars and Venus invading the Grand Pivot's upper general. Within a month Ma Sui died.

sentences.zh: 廢朝四日，詔京兆尹韓臯監護喪事，嗣吳王獻為吊祭贈赗使，冊贈太尉，謚曰莊武。

translations.literal: Court mourning was suspended four days; an edict ordered Capital Intendant Han Gao to supervise funeral affairs; Heir of Wu Wang Xian as condolence and gift envoy; he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Commandant with posthumous title Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning was suspended four days. An edict ordered Capital Intendant Han Gao to supervise funeral affairs. Heir of Wu Wang Xian as condolence and gift envoy. He was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Commandant with posthumous title Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 子匯、暢。

translations.literal: Sons Hui and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Hui and Chang.

sentences.zh: 暢以父廕累遷至鴻臚少卿，留京師。

translations.literal: Chang through his father's shadow was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and remained at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chang through his father's shadow was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and remained at the capital.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，燧討田悅於山東，時歲旱，京師括率商戶，人心甚搖。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong Sui attacked Tian Yue in Shandong; at that time the year was drought; the capital levied merchants; people's hearts were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianzhong Ma Sui attacked Tian Yue in Shandong. At that time the year was drought. The capital levied merchants. People's hearts were greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔留鎮幽州兵，多離散入南山為盜。

translations.literal: Fengxiang garrison troops left at You Prefecture mostly scattered into the Southern Hills as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang garrison troops left at You Prefecture mostly scattered into the Southern Hills as bandits.

sentences.zh: 殿中丞李雲端與其黨袁封、單超俊、李誠信、冀信等與暢善，因飲食聚會，言時事將危；

translations.literal: Palace censor Li Yunduan with his faction Yuan Feng, Shan Chaojun, Li Chengxin, Ji Xin and others were friendly with Chang; because of feasting and gathering they spoke that the times would soon be perilous;
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor Li Yunduan with his faction Yuan Feng, Shan Chaojun, Li Chengxin, Ji Xin and others were friendly with Chang. Because of feasting and gathering they spoke that the times would soon be perilous.

sentences.zh: 暢乃遣家人溫靖與父書，具陳利害，可班師還鎮。

translations.literal: Chang then sent his household member Wen Jing to write his father a letter fully stating benefit and harm—that he could withdraw the army and return to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Chang then sent his household member Wen Jing to write his father a letter fully stating benefit and harm—that he could withdraw the army and return to garrison.

sentences.zh: 燧怒，執靖具奏其狀，令兄炫執暢請罪。

translations.literal: Sui was angry, seized Jing and fully reported the situation, ordered his elder brother Xuan to seize Chang and ask guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui was angry, seized Wen Jing and fully reported the situation, ordered his elder brother Xuan to seize Chang and ask guilt.

sentences.zh: 德宗以燧方討賊，不竟其事，誅雲端等十一人，敕炫就第杖暢三十，上於是罷括率之令。

translations.literal: Dezong because Sui was attacking bandits did not pursue the matter to the end; Yunduan and eleven others were executed; an edict ordered Xuan to go to the residence and cane Chang thirty strokes; the emperor thereupon abolished the levy order.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong because Ma Sui was attacking bandits did not pursue the matter to the end. Yunduan and eleven others were executed. An edict ordered Xuan to go to the residence and cane Chang thirty strokes. The emperor thereupon abolished the levy order.

sentences.zh: 燧貲貨甲天下，燧既卒，暢承舊業，屢為豪幸邀取。

translations.literal: Sui's wealth and goods were foremost under Heaven; once Sui died Chang inherited the old enterprise and was repeatedly taken from by powerful favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui's wealth and goods were foremost under Heaven. Once Sui died Chang inherited the old enterprise and was repeatedly taken from by powerful favorites.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，中尉楊誌廉諷暢令獻田園第宅，順宗復賜暢。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan Chief Eunuch Yang Zhilian hinted Chang should present fields, gardens, and mansions; Emperor Shunzong again bestowed on Chang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhenyuan Chief Eunuch Yang Zhilian hinted Chang should present fields, gardens, and mansions. Emperor Shunzong again bestowed on Chang.

sentences.zh: 初為匯妻所訴，析其產，中貴又逼取，仍指使施於佛寺，暢不敢吝；

translations.literal: At first sued by Hui's wife, his property was divided; palace favorites again forced taking and still directed spending on Buddhist temples—Chang dared not be stingy;
translations.idiomatic: At first sued by Hui's wife, his property was divided. Palace favorites again forced taking and still directed spending on Buddhist temples—Chang dared not be stingy.

sentences.zh: 晚年財產並盡，身歿之後，諸子無室可居，以至凍餒。

translations.literal: in later years property was all gone; after his body died his sons had no room to dwell, even to freezing and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: In later years property was all gone. After his body died his sons had no room to dwell, even to freezing and hunger.

sentences.zh: 今奉誠園亭館，即暢舊第也。

translations.literal: Now the Fengcheng garden pavilion and hall is Chang's old residence.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Fengcheng garden pavilion and hall is Chang's old residence.

sentences.zh: 暢終少府監，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: Chang ended as director of the Palace Workshop and was posthumously given Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ended as director of the Palace Workshop and was posthumously given Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子繼祖，以祖廕，四歲為太子舍人，累遷至殿中少監，年三十七卒。

translations.literal: Son Jizu through his grandfather's shadow at four years was Crown Prince's attendant, repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Palace Directorate, and died at thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Son Jizu through his grandfather's shadow at four years was Crown Prince's attendant, repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Palace Directorate, and died at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 炫，字弱翁，燧之仲兄，少以儒學聞於時，隱居蘇門山，不應辟召。

translations.literal: Xuan, styled Ruoweng, Sui's second elder brother, in youth was famed for Confucian learning and lived in seclusion on Mount Sumen, not responding to summons.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, styled Ruoweng, Ma Sui's second elder brother, in youth was famed for Confucian learning and lived in seclusion on Mount Sumen, not responding to summons.

sentences.zh: 至德中，李光弼鎮太原，辟為掌書記、試大理評事、監察御史，歷侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era Li Guangbi garrisoned Taiyuan and recruited him as chief secretary, trial grand court judge, and censor; he served as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhide era Li Guangbi garrisoned Taiyuan and recruited him as chief secretary, trial grand court judge, and censor. He served as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 常參謀議，光弼甚重之，奏授比部、刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He often joined in counsel; Guangbi greatly valued him and memorialized appointing him director of the Revenue and Punishments bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He often joined in counsel. Li Guangbi greatly valued him and memorialized appointing him director of the Revenue and Punishments bureaus.

sentences.zh: 田神功鎮汴州，奏授節度判官、檢校兵部郎中。

translations.literal: When Tian Shengon garrisoned Bian Prefecture he was memorialized as military commissioner's judge and acting director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Shengon garrisoned Bian Prefecture he was memorialized as military commissioner's judge and acting director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉連州刺史，征拜吏部郎中，又出為閬州刺史，入為大理少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred prefect of Lian Prefecture, summoned as director of the Ministry of Personnel, again went out as prefect of Lang Prefecture, and entered as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred prefect of Lian Prefecture, summoned as director of the Ministry of Personnel, again went out as prefect of Lang Prefecture, and entered as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 建中初，為潤州刺史，黜陟使柳載以清白聞，征拜太子右庶子，遷左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianzhong he was Run Prefecture prefect; promotion commissioner Liu Zai because of pure reputation summoned him as Right Crown Prince's aide and transferred Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianzhong he was Run Prefecture prefect. Promotion commissioner Liu Zai because of pure reputation summoned him as Right Crown Prince's aide and transferred Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 弟燧為司徒，以親比拜刑部侍郎，以疾辭，改兵部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Younger brother Sui was Grand Mentor; because of kinship he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Punishments; because of illness he declined and was changed to Minister of War retiring.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Ma Sui was Grand Mentor. Because of kinship he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Punishments. Because of illness he declined and was changed to Minister of War retiring.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年卒，時年七十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenyuan he died; at that time he was seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenyuan he died. At that time he was seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：燧雄勇強力，常先計後戰，又善誓師，將戰，親自號令，士無不慷慨感動，戰皆決死，未嘗折北，謀得兵勝，冠於一時。

translations.literal: The historian says: Sui was bold, brave, and strong; he always planned before fighting; he was also good at rallying the army; before battle he personally gave commands and the men without exception were stirred to generosity; in battle they all fought to the death; he never suffered defeat; stratagem obtained, troops won—foremost in his age.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Ma Sui was bold, brave, and strong. He always planned before fighting. He was also good at rallying the army. Before battle he personally gave commands and the men without exception were stirred to generosity. In battle they all fought to the death. He never suffered defeat. Stratagem obtained, troops won—foremost in his age.

sentences.zh: 然力能擒田悅而不取，納蕃帥之偽款而保其必盟；

translations.literal: Yet though his strength could capture Tian Yue he did not take him; he accepted the Tibetan commander's false submission and assured they would surely ally;
translations.idiomatic: Yet though his strength could capture Tian Yue he did not take him. He accepted the Tibetan commander's false submission and assured they would surely ally.

sentences.zh: 平涼之會，大臣幾陷，關畿搖動，此謂才有余而心不至，議者惜而恨之。

translations.literal: at the Pingliang meeting great ministers nearly fell; the capital region was shaken—this is called talent in surplus but heart not arriving; commentators regretted and resented it.
translations.idiomatic: At the Pingliang meeting great ministers nearly fell. The capital region was shaken—this is called talent in surplus but heart not arriving. Commentators regretted and resented it.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊

translations.literal: Hun Jian
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian

sentences.zh: 渾瑊，臯蘭州人也，本鐵勒九姓部落之渾部也。

translations.literal: Hun Jian was a native of Gao Prefecture; originally of the Hun tribe among the Tiele Nine Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian was a native of Gao Prefecture. He originally came from the Hun tribe among the Tiele Nine Surnames.

sentences.zh: 高祖大俟利發渾阿貪支，貞觀中為臯蘭州刺史。

translations.literal: Great-great-grandfather the grand chieftain Hun A'chenzhi in the Zhenguan era was Gao Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Great-great-grandfather the grand chieftain Hun A'chenzhi in the Zhenguan era was Gao Prefecture prefect.

sentences.zh: 曾祖元慶、祖大壽、父釋之，皆代為臯蘭都督。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Yuanqing, grandfather Dashou, and father Shizhi all for generations were Gao Prefecture governors.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Yuanqing, grandfather Dashou, and father Shizhi all for generations were Gao Prefecture governors.

sentences.zh: 大壽，開元初歷左領衛中郎將、太子仆同正。

translations.literal: Dashou, at the start of Kaiyuan served as Left Leading Guard middle commander and Crown Prince's steward of equal rank.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou, at the start of Kaiyuan served as Left Leading Guard middle commander and Crown Prince's steward of equal rank.

sentences.zh: 釋之，少有武藝，從朔方軍，積戰功於邊上，累遷至開府儀同三司、試太常卿、寧朔郡王。

translations.literal: Shizhi in youth had martial arts; he followed the Shuofang Army, accumulated battle merit on the frontier, and was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Illustrious Affairs, acting Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and Prince of Ningsuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi in youth had martial arts. He followed the Shuofang Army, accumulated battle merit on the frontier, and was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Illustrious Affairs, acting Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and Prince of Ningsuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 廣德中，與吐蕃戰，沒於靈武，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the Guangde era he fought Tibet and died at Lingwu; he was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangde era he fought Tibet and died at Lingwu. He was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 瑊本名曰進，年十余歲即善騎射，隨父戰伐，破賀魯部，下石保城，收龍駒島，勇冠諸軍，累授折衝果毅。

translations.literal: Jian's original name was Jin; at more than ten years he was already skilled at riding and shooting; he followed his father in campaigns, broke the Helu tribe, took Xiabao Fort, recovered Longju Island—brave foremost among the armies—and was repeatedly appointed Victorious Charge commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's original name was Jin. At more than ten years he was already skilled at riding and shooting. He followed his father in campaigns, broke the Helu tribe, took Xiabao Fort, recovered Longju Island—brave foremost among the armies—and was repeatedly appointed Victorious Charge commander.

sentences.zh: 後節度使安思順遣瑊提偏師深入葛祿部，經狐媚磧，略特羅斯山，大破阿布思部；

translations.literal: Later Military Commissioner An Sishun sent Jian leading a detached army deep into the Gelu tribe, passed Humei Desert, raided Teluosi Mountain, and greatly broke Abu Si's tribe;
translations.idiomatic: Later Military Commissioner An Sishun sent Jian leading a detached army deep into the Gelu tribe, passed Humei Desert, raised Teluosi Mountain, and greatly broke Abu Si's tribe.

sentences.zh: 又與諸軍城永清柵、天安軍，遷中郎將。

translations.literal: he again with the armies walled Yongqing Palisade and Tian'an Army and was promoted middle commander.
translations.idiomatic: He again with the armies walled Yongqing Palisade and Tian'an Army and was promoted middle commander.

sentences.zh: 安祿山構逆，瑊從李光弼出師河北，定諸郡邑。

translations.literal: When An Lushu plotted rebellion Jian followed Li Guangbi out with the army to Hebei and settled the commanderies and districts.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushu plotted rebellion Jian followed Li Guangbi out with the army to Hebei and settled the commanderies and districts.

sentences.zh: 賊將有李立節者，素稱驍勇，與瑊格鬥，臨陣斬之，遷右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Among bandit generals there was one Li Lijie famed as fierce and brave; he grappled with Jian in battle and Jian beheaded him on the field; he was promoted Right Xiaoqi Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Among bandit generals there was one Li Lijie famed as fierce and brave. He grappled with Jian in battle and Jian beheaded him on the field. He was promoted Right Xiaoqi Guard general.

sentences.zh: 既而肅宗即位於靈武，瑊統兵赴行在，至天德，遇蕃軍入寇，瑊擊敗之。

translations.literal: Then Emperor Suzong ascended at Lingwu; Jian led troops to the mobile court; reaching Tiande he met Tibetan troops entering to raid and Jian defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Suzong ascended at Lingwu. Jian led troops to the mobile court. Reaching Tiande he met Tibetan troops entering to raid and Jian defeated them.

sentences.zh: 從郭子儀收兩京，瑊討安慶緒，破賊於新鄉。

translations.literal: Following Guo Ziyi in recovering the two capitals Jian attacked An Qingxu and broke the bandits at Xinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Following Guo Ziyi in recovering the two capitals Jian attacked An Qingxu and broke the bandits at Xinxiang.

sentences.zh: 改檢校太仆卿，充武鋒軍使。

translations.literal: He was changed acting Grand Minister of Steeds and made Wufeng Army commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed acting Grand Minister of Steeds and made Wufeng Army commander.

sentences.zh: 又從仆固懷恩討史朝義，前後數十戰。

translations.literal: He again followed Pugu Huai'en to attack Shi Chaoyi—before and after several tens of battles.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Pugu Huai'en to attack Shi Chaoyi—before and after several tens of battles.

sentences.zh: 朝義平，加開府儀同三司、太常卿，賜實封二百戶。

translations.literal: When Chaoyi was pacified he was promoted Grand General of Illustrious Affairs and Grand Minister of Ceremonies and given two hundred households of real enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoyi was pacified he was promoted Grand General of Illustrious Affairs and Grand Minister of Ceremonies and given two hundred households of real enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 及懷恩謀亂，令子歊與瑊率軍圍榆次，朔方將殺歊，瑊率所部歸郭子儀。

translations.literal: When Huai'en plotted rebellion he ordered his son Yang and Jian to lead troops and besiege Yuci; Shuofang generals killed Yang; Jian led his division back to Guo Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'en plotted rebellion he ordered his son Yang and Jian to lead troops and besiege Yuci. Shuofang generals killed Yang. Jian led his division back to Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 會瑊父釋之戰死，又起復本官，為朔方行營左廂兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Jian's father Shizhi died in battle he again rose from mourning to his original office and was Shuofang mobile-camp Left Wing military envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian's father Shizhi died in battle he again rose from mourning to his original office and was Shuofang mobile-camp Left Wing military envoy.

sentences.zh: 從子儀討吐蕃於邠州。

translations.literal: He followed Ziyi to attack Tibet at Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Guo Ziyi to attack Tibet at Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以功加御史中丞。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was promoted censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 軍還，盛秋於邠。

translations.literal: The army returned and garrisoned autumn defense at Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The army returned and garrisoned autumn defense at Bin.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃大入寇，至奉天，瑊拒戰於漠谷，大破蕃軍，以功加太子賓客，復屯於奉天。

translations.literal: When Tibet greatly entered to raid and reached Fengtian Jian resisted at Mogu Valley and greatly broke the Tibetan army; for merit he was promoted Crown Prince's guest and again garrisoned at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet greatly entered to raid and reached Fengtian Jian resisted at Mogu Valley and greatly broke the Tibetan army. For merit he was promoted Crown Prince's guest and again garrisoned at Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 華州周智光反，子儀奉詔討之，令瑊領馬步萬人攻下同州。

translations.literal: When Hua Prefecture Zhou Zhiguang rebelled Ziyi received orders to attack him and ordered Jian to lead ten thousand foot and horse to attack and take Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Prefecture Zhou Zhiguang rebelled Guo Ziyi received orders to attack him and ordered Jian to lead ten thousand foot and horse to attack and take Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 智光平，詔以邠、寧、慶三州隸朔方軍，子儀領之；

translations.literal: When Zhiguang was pacified an edict made Bin, Ning, and Qing three prefectures subordinate to the Shuofang Army and Ziyi led them;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiguang was pacified an edict made Bin, Ning, and Qing three prefectures subordinate to the Shuofang Army and Guo Ziyi led them.

sentences.zh: 子儀令瑊先率兵至邠州，便於宜祿縣防秋。

translations.literal: Ziyi ordered Jian first to lead troops to Bin Prefecture and then garrison autumn defense at Yilu County.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi ordered Jian first to lead troops to Bin Prefecture and then garrison autumn defense at Yilu County.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，加兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was promoted concurrently Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was promoted concurrently Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 大歷七年，吐蕃大寇邊，瑊與涇原節度使馬璘會兵，大破蕃賊於黃菩原。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali Tibet greatly raided the frontier; Jian with Jingyuan military commissioner Ma Lin joined armies and greatly broke Tibetan bandits at Huangpu Plain.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dali Tibet greatly raided the frontier. Jian with Jingyuan military commissioner Ma Lin joined armies and greatly broke Tibetan bandits at Huangpu Plain.

sentences.zh: 自是，每年常戍於長武城，臨盛秋。

translations.literal: From this each year he regularly garrisoned at Changwu Fort at the height of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: From this each year he regularly garrisoned at Changwu Fort at the height of autumn.

sentences.zh: 十一年，領邠州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he led Bin Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he led Bin Prefecture prefect.

sentences.zh: 其年，吐蕃入寇州方渠、懷安等鎮，瑊擊卻之。

translations.literal: That year Tibet entered to raid Fangqu, Huai'an and other garrisons; Jian beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tibet entered to raid Fangqu, Huai'an and other garrisons. Jian beat them back.

sentences.zh: 十二年，子儀入朝，令瑊知邠寧慶三州兵馬留後。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Ziyi entered court and ordered Jian to know Bin, Ning, and Qing three prefectures' troops as regent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Guo Ziyi entered court and ordered Jian to know Bin, Ning, and Qing three prefectures' troops as regent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，回紇侵太原，破鮑防軍，北歸，頗為邊患。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Uyghurs invaded Taiyuan and broke Bao Fang's army; returning north they were much a frontier trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Uyghurs invaded Taiyuan and broke Bao Fang's army. Returning north they were much a frontier trouble.

sentences.zh: 以瑊為石嶺關已南諸軍都知兵馬使，率兵掎角逐之，虜騎引退。

translations.literal: Jian was made commander knowing troops of all armies south of Shiling Pass; he led troops to flank and pursue and the barbarian cavalry withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was made commander knowing troops of all armies south of Shiling Pass. He led troops to flank and pursue and the barbarian cavalry withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，加檢校工部尚書、單於副都護、振武軍使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he was promoted acting Minister of Works, Shanyu vice-protector, and Zhenwu Army commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year he was promoted acting Minister of Works, Shanyu vice-protector, and Zhenwu Army commander.

sentences.zh: 十四年，郭子儀拜太尉，號尚父，分所管內別置三節度，以瑊兼單於大都護，充振武軍、東受降城、鎮北大都護府、綏銀麟勝等軍州節度副大使知節度使事、管內支度營田等使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Guo Ziyi was made Grand Commandant and styled Exalted Father; within what he administered three military commissions were separately established; Jian concurrently held Shanyu grand protectorate, deputy Zhenwu Army, Eastern Shouxiang City, and Zhenbei grand protectorate offices, Sui-Yin-Lin-Sheng and other army-prefecture military commission deputy ambassador knowing military commissioner affairs and circuit internal support, garrison-fields and other commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Guo Ziyi was made Grand Commandant and styled Exalted Father. Within what he administered three military commissions were separately established. Jian concurrently held Shanyu grand protectorate, deputy Zhenwu Army, Eastern Shouxiang City, and Zhenbei grand protectorate offices, Sui-Yin-Lin-Sheng and other army-prefecture military commission deputy ambassador knowing military commissioner affairs and circuit internal support, garrison-fields and other commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其年，復以崔寧為朔方節度使，領子儀舊管，征瑊為左金吾衛大將軍，兼左街使。

translations.literal: That year Cui Ning was again made Shuofang military commissioner leading Ziyi's old administration; Jian was summoned as Left Golden Guard great general and concurrently Left Street commander.
translations.idiomatic: That year Cui Ning was again made Shuofang military commissioner leading Guo Ziyi's old administration. Jian was summoned as Left Golden Guard great general and concurrently Left Street commander.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，李希烈遣間諜詐為瑊書與希烈交通，瑊奏其狀，上特保證之，仍賜瑊馬一匹並鞍轡，錦采二百匹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong Li Xilie sent spies feigning as Jian's letter communicating with Xilie; Jian reported the situation; the emperor specially guaranteed him and still gave Jian one horse with saddle and trappings and two hundred bolts of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianzhong Li Xilie sent spies feigning as Jian's letter communicating with Xilie. Jian reported the situation. The emperor specially guaranteed him and still gave Jian one horse with saddle and trappings and two hundred bolts of brocade.

sentences.zh: 時以普王為荊襄等道兵馬元帥討李希烈，大開府幕，以瑊檢校戶部尚書、御史大夫，充中軍都虞候。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Pu was grand marshal of Jingxiang and other routes' troops attacking Li Xilie and greatly opened the headquarters staff; Jian was made acting Minister of Revenue, censor-in-chief, and central army chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Pu was grand marshal of Jingxiang and other routes' troops attacking Li Xilie and greatly opened the headquarters staff. Jian was made acting Minister of Revenue, censor-in-chief, and central army chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 會涇師亂，德宗幸奉天，後三日，瑊率家人子弟自京城至，乃署為行在都虞候、檢校兵部尚書、京畿渭北節度觀察使。

translations.literal: When the Jing troops mutinied Dezong went to Fengtian; three days later Jian led family members and sons and younger brothers from the capital to arrive; he was then appointed mobile-court chief adjutant, acting Minister of War, and Jingji-Weibei military observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing troops mutinied Emperor Dezong went to Fengtian. Three days later Jian led family members and sons and younger brothers from the capital to arrive. He was then appointed mobile-court chief adjutant, acting Minister of War, and Jingji-Weibei military observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 居數日，邠寧節度使韓遊瑰與慶州刺史論惟明統兵三千，自乾陵北過，赴醴泉以拒硃泚。

translations.literal: After several days Binning military commissioner Han Yougui with Qing Prefecture prefect Lun Weiming leading three thousand troops from north of Qianling passed through to go to Liquan to resist Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Binning military commissioner Han Yougui with Qing Prefecture prefect Lun Weiming leading three thousand troops from north of Qianling passed through to go to Liquan to resist Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 會諜報泚已出兵，帝遽令追遊瑰兵，才至奉天，賊軍果至。

translations.literal: When spies reported Ci had already sent out troops the emperor hastily ordered Yougui's troops pursued; they had just reached Fengtian when bandit troops indeed arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When spies reported Zhu Ci had already sent out troops the emperor hastily ordered Yougui's troops pursued. They had just reached Fengtian when bandit troops indeed arrived.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰等戰於城東，王師不利，遂乘勝奔突，將入，官軍與賊隔門相持，自卯至午，殺傷頗甚。

translations.literal: Yougui and the others fought east of the city; the imperial army was unfavorable; they then took victory and rushed forward intending to enter; the imperial army and bandits faced one another across the gate from mao hour to wu hour; casualties were considerable.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui and the others fought east of the city. The imperial army was unfavorable. They then took victory and rushed forward intending to enter. The imperial army and bandits faced one another across the gate from mao hour to wu hour. Casualties were considerable.

sentences.zh: 門內有草車數乘，瑊令推車塞門，焚之以外禦，乘火力戰，賊方解去，然重圍已合。

translations.literal: Inside the gate were several hay carts; Jian ordered carts pushed to block the gate and burned them to defend outward; riding the fire's strength they fought; the bandits then withdrew, yet the heavy encirclement was already complete.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the gate were several hay carts. Jian ordered carts pushed to block the gate and burned them to defend outward. Riding the fire's strength they fought. The bandits then withdrew, yet the heavy encirclement was already complete.

sentences.zh: 賊大修攻具，以僧法堅為匠師，毀佛寺房宇以為梯櫓。

translations.literal: The bandits greatly repaired siege engines; they took the monk Fajian as master craftsman and destroyed Buddhist temple buildings to make ladders and siege towers.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits greatly repaired siege engines. They took the monk Fajian as master craftsman and destroyed Buddhist temple buildings to make ladders and siege towers.

sentences.zh: 是月，賊自丁未至辛未，四面攻城，晝夜矢石不絕，瑊隨機應敵，僅能自固。

translations.literal: That month from dingwei to xinwei they attacked the city on four sides day and night; arrows and stones without cease; Jian responded to the enemy as occasion arose and barely could hold himself.
translations.idiomatic: That month from dingwei to xinwei they attacked the city on four sides day and night. Arrows and stones without cease. Jian responded to the enemy as occasion arose and barely could hold himself.

sentences.zh: 十一月，靈武節度使杜希全、鹽州刺史戴休顏、夏州刺史常春合兵六千人赴難。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Lingwu military commissioner Du Xiquan, Yan Prefecture prefect Dai Xiuyan, and Xia Prefecture prefect Chang Chun joined armies of six thousand men to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Lingwu military commissioner Du Xiquan, Yan Prefecture prefect Dai Xiuyan, and Xia Prefecture prefect Chang Chun joined armies of six thousand men to go to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 將至，上議其所向，宰相盧杞、白誌貞以漠谷路為便。

translations.literal: When about to arrive the emperor discussed where they should go; Grand Councilors Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen thought the Mogu route convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When about to arrive the emperor discussed where they should go. Grand Councilors Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen thought the Mogu route convenient.

sentences.zh: 瑊曰：「漠谷險隘，必為賊所邀，不若取乾陵北過，附柏城而行，便取城東北雞子堆下營，與城中掎角相應，且分賊勢，硃泚必不更於陵寢往來。」

translations.literal: Jian said: "Mogu is narrow and perilous; bandits will surely intercept; better take north of Qianling, follow Cypress City and march, then camp below Jizidui northeast of the city, respond in pincers with the city, and also divide bandit strength—Zhu Ci surely will not again pass to and fro at the imperial tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Mogu is narrow and perilous. Bandits will surely intercept. Better take north of Qianling, follow Cypress City and march, then camp below Jizidui northeast of the city, respond in pincers with the city, and also divide bandit strength—Zhu Ci surely will not again pass to and fro at the imperial tombs."

sentences.zh: 杞曰：「漠谷路近，若慮逆賊邀擊，即出兵應接，若取乾陵路，恐驚陵寢。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "The Mogu route is near; if one fears rebel bandits intercepting, then send troops to respond; if one takes the Qianling route one fears disturbing the imperial tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi said, "The Mogu route is near. If one fears rebel bandits intercepting, then send troops to respond. If one takes the Qianling route one fears disturbing the imperial tombs."

sentences.zh: 瑊曰：「今硃泚圍城，斬伐柏城，以夜繼晝，驚動已多。

translations.literal: Jian said: "Now Zhu Ci besieges the city and cuts cypress from the tomb city, night continuing day—disturbance already much.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Now Zhu Ci besieges the city and cuts cypress from the tomb city, night continuing day—disturbance already much.

sentences.zh: 今城中危急，佇望救軍，唯希全等率行赴難，安危是賴，所系非輕，制置不宜差跌。

translations.literal: Now peril in the city; looking morning and evening for rescue troops—only Xiquan and others lead troops to go to the rescue; safety and danger rely on this; what is tied is not light; disposition should not err.
translations.idiomatic: Now peril in the city. Looking morning and evening for rescue troops—only Du Xiquan and others lead troops to go to the rescue. Safety and danger rely on this. What is tied is not light. Disposition should not err.

sentences.zh: 但令希全等於雞子堆下營，固守善地，賊泚可以計破也。」

translations.literal: Only order Xiquan and others to camp below Jizidui, firmly hold good ground—bandit Ci can be broken by plan."
translations.idiomatic: Only order Du Xiquan and others to camp below Jizidui, firmly hold good ground—bandit Ci can be broken by plan."

sentences.zh: 盧杞等曰：「陛下以順討逆，不可自驚陵寢。」

translations.literal: Lu Qi and others said: "Your Majesty with compliance attacks rebellion—one cannot oneself disturb the imperial tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi and others said, "Your Majesty with compliance attacks rebellion—one cannot oneself disturb the imperial tombs."

sentences.zh: 白誌貞從而贊之，上從杞議。

translations.literal: Bai Zhizhen followed and praised it; the emperor followed Qi's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zhizhen followed and praised it. The emperor followed Lu Qi's plan.

sentences.zh: 希全等進至漠谷，果為賊軍邀擊，奪據水口，乘高以大弩、巨石左右夾擊，殺傷頗甚；

translations.literal: Xiquan and others advanced to Mogu and indeed were intercepted by bandit troops; they seized the water mouth; riding high ground they struck left and right with great crossbows and boulders; casualties were considerable;
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiquan and others advanced to Mogu and indeed were intercepted by bandit troops. They seized the water mouth. Riding high ground they struck left and right with great crossbows and boulders. Casualties were considerable.

sentences.zh: 城中出兵應援，亦為賊挫銳而退。

translations.literal: the city sent troops to respond and were also broken in sharpness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The city sent troops to respond and were also broken in sharpness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 希全等各歸還本鎮，賊攻城逾急，壕塹環之。

translations.literal: Xiquan and others each returned to their original garrisons; bandit siege grew more urgent; moats and ramparts ringed them.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiquan and others each returned to their original garrisons. Bandit siege grew more urgent. Moats and ramparts ringed them.

sentences.zh: 旬日，復偏攻東北角，矢石亂入，晝夜如雨，城中死傷者甚眾。

translations.literal: After ten days they again partially attacked the northeast corner; arrows and stones entered in confusion day and night like rain; dead and wounded in the city were very many.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days they again partially attacked the northeast corner. Arrows and stones entered in confusion day and night like rain. Dead and wounded in the city were very many.

sentences.zh: 重圍救絕，芻粟俱盡，城中伺賊休息，輒遣人城外捃拾樵采以進禦。

translations.literal: The heavy encirclement rescue cut off; fodder and grain all exhausted; in the city watching bandits rest they then sent men outside the city to gather firewood and fuel to supply defense.
translations.idiomatic: The heavy encirclement rescue cut off. Fodder and grain all exhausted. In the city watching bandits rest they then sent men outside the city to gather firewood and fuel to supply defense.

sentences.zh: 人心危蹙，上與瑊對泣。

translations.literal: Men's hearts were perilous and tight; the emperor and Jian faced one another weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Men's hearts were perilous and tight. The emperor and Jian faced one another weeping.

sentences.zh: 賊泚北據乾陵，下瞰城內，身衣黃衣，蔽以翟扇，前後左右，皆硃紫閹官，宴賜拜舞，紛紜旁午。

translations.literal: Bandit Ci north held Qianling overlooking the city; his body wore yellow robes screened with pheasant fans; before and behind left and right were all vermilion and purple eunuch officials; feasts, gifts, bows and dances were confused noon and midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit Zhu Ci north held Qianling overlooking the city. His body wore yellow robes screened with pheasant fans. Before and behind left and right were all vermilion and purple eunuch officials. Feasts, gifts, bows and dances were confused noon and midnight.

sentences.zh: 城中動息，賊俯窺之，慢辭戲侮，以為破在漏刻之頃，時令騎將環城招公卿、士庶，責以不識天命。

translations.literal: The city's movements and breaths the bandits looked down and spied; slow words mocked and insulted; they thought breaking was in the drip of a clepsydra; at times they ordered cavalry generals to circle the city summoning ministers and commoners, blaming them for not knowing Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The city's movements and breaths the bandits looked down and spied. Slow words mocked and insulted. They thought breaking was in the drip of a clepsydra. At times they ordered cavalry generals to circle the city summoning ministers and commoners, blaming them for not knowing Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 十五日，賊造雲橋成，闊數十丈，以巨輪為腳，推之使前，施濕氈生牛革，多懸水囊以為障，直指城東北隅，兩旁構木為廬，冒以牛革，回環相屬，負土運薪於其下，以填壕塹，矢石不能傷。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day the bandits finished the cloud bridge—several tens of zhang wide—with great wheels as feet pushed forward; wet felt and raw ox hide were applied; many hanging water bags as screens; it pointed straight at the northeast corner of the city; on both sides they built wooden sheds covered with ox hide linked in rings; they carried earth and hauled firewood below to fill moats and ramparts—arrows and stones could not harm.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day the bandits finished the cloud bridge—several tens of zhang wide—with great wheels as feet pushed forward. Wet felt and raw ox hide were applied. Many hanging water bags as screens. It pointed straight at the northeast corner of the city. On both sides they built wooden sheds covered with ox hide linked in rings. They carried earth and hauled firewood below to fill moats and ramparts—arrows and stones could not harm.

sentences.zh: 城中恟懼，相顧失色。

translations.literal: In the city there was panic; they looked at one another and paled.
translations.idiomatic: In the city there was panic. They looked at one another and paled.

sentences.zh: 上召瑊勉諭之，令賫空名告身自御史大夫、實封五百已下者千余軸，募諸軍突將敢死之士以當之；

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Jian and encouraged him; he ordered him to carry blank commission scrolls from Grand Censor down to five hundred households of real enfeoffment more than a thousand scrolls; recruit from the armies daring vanguard and death-defying men to meet it;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Jian and encouraged him. He ordered him to carry blank commission scrolls from Grand Censor down to five hundred households of real enfeoffment more than a thousand scrolls. Recruit from the armies daring vanguard and death-defying men to meet it.

sentences.zh: 兼賜瑊御筆一管，當戰勝，量其功伐，即署其名授之，不足者，筆書其身，因命以位。

translations.literal: he also gave Jian one imperial brush; when battle was won, measuring their merit in battle, then sign their names and grant them; where insufficient, the brush wrote on their bodies and then ordered by rank.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave Jian one imperial brush. When battle was won, measuring their merit in battle, then sign their names and grant them. Where insufficient, the brush wrote on their bodies and then ordered by rank.

sentences.zh: 仍謂瑊曰：「朕便與卿別，更不用對來，縱有急切，令馬承倩在卿處，但令附奏。」

translations.literal: He again said to Jian: "I then part with you; no more need face audience; even if urgent, order Ma Chengqian at your place—only order him attach memorial."
translations.idiomatic: He again said to Jian, "I then part with you. No more need face audience. Even if urgent, order Ma Chengqian at your place—only order him attach memorial."

sentences.zh: 瑊俯伏嗚咽，上亦悲慟不自勝，撫瑊背而遣之。

translations.literal: Jian prostrated himself sobbing; the emperor also grieved beyond bearing; he stroked Jian's back and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Jian prostrated himself sobbing. The emperor also grieved beyond bearing. He stroked Jian's back and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 前一日，瑊與防城使侯仲莊揣雲橋來路，先鑿地道，下可深丈余，上積馬糞，深五六尺。

translations.literal: The day before Jian with defense commissioner Hou Zhongzhuang measured the cloud bridge's coming route; they first dug an underground passage more than a zhang deep below; above they piled horse dung five or six chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: The day before Jian with defense commissioner Hou Zhongzhuang measured the cloud bridge's coming route. They first dug an underground passage more than a zhang deep below. Above they piled horse dung five or six chi deep.

sentences.zh: 次二日，即令爇火，次一日復下柴薪夜燒之，平明，火焰高於城壘。

translations.literal: The next day they then ordered fire lit; the next day again piled firewood and burned at night; at dawn flames were higher than the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they then ordered fire lit. The next day again piled firewood and burned at night. At dawn flames were higher than the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 是時，北風正急，賊乃隨風推橋以薄城下，賊三千余人相繼而登。

translations.literal: At that time the north wind was just strong; the bandits then pushed the bridge with the wind to press the city; more than three thousand bandits in succession climbed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the north wind was just strong. The bandits then pushed the bridge with the wind to press the city. More than three thousand bandits in succession climbed.

sentences.zh: 城上士卒皆久寒餒，又少甲胄，瑊但感激誠厲之。

translations.literal: Soldiers on the wall had long been cold and hungry and also had little armor; Jian only stirred them with gratitude and earnest exhortation.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers on the wall had long been cold and hungry and also had little armor. Jian only stirred them with gratitude and earnest exhortation.

sentences.zh: 以饑弱之眾，當劇賊之鋒，雖力戰應敵，人憂不濟，公卿已下，仰首祝天。

translations.literal: With hungry and weak masses facing fierce bandit points—though they fought hard responding to the enemy men feared it would not succeed; from ministers down they raised heads praying to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: With hungry and weak masses facing fierce bandit points—though they fought hard responding to the enemy men feared it would not succeed. From ministers down they raised heads praying to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 賊徒至地道所，橋腳偏陷，不能進。

translations.literal: When bandit masses reached where the underground passage was the bridge feet partially sank and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When bandit masses reached where the underground passage was the bridge feet partially sank and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 須臾，風回焰轉，雲橋焚為灰燼，賊焚死者數千，城中歡噪振地。

translations.literal: In a moment the wind turned and flames turned; the cloud bridge burned to ash; bandits burned dead numbered several thousand; in the city shouts shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the wind turned and flames turned. The cloud bridge burned to ash. Bandits burned dead numbered several thousand. In the city shouts shook the earth.

sentences.zh: 時瑊中流矢，遽自拔之，血流沾沫，格鬥不已，初不言瘡痛，以激士心。

translations.literal: At that time Jian was struck by a flowing arrow; he hastily pulled it out himself; blood flowed smeared with foam; he grappled without cease; at first he did not speak of wound pain—to stir men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jian was struck by a flowing arrow. He hastily pulled it out himself. Blood flowed smeared with foam. He grappled without cease. At first he did not speak of wound pain—to stir men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 是日，上先授瑊二子官，余授將校有差。

translations.literal: That day the emperor first granted Jian's two sons office; the rest granted officers and commanders with differences.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor first granted Jian's two sons office. The rest granted officers and commandants with differences.

sentences.zh: 賊又別造雲橋，周以重鐵，方就，而朔方節度使李懷光自魏縣行營赴難，先遣兵馬使張韶入奏。

translations.literal: The bandits again separately made a cloud bridge ringed with heavy iron; just as it was finished Shuofang military commissioner Li Huai'guang from Wei County mobile camp went to the rescue and first sent military envoy Zhang Shao to enter memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits again separately made a cloud bridge ringed with heavy iron. Just as it was finished Shuofang military commissioner Li Huai'guang from Wei County mobile camp went to the rescue and first sent military envoy Zhang Shao to enter memorial.

sentences.zh: 韶至奉天，與賊填塹者相雜，臨城忽大呼，謂城上曰：「我李懷光使也，懷光自河北領大軍至矣。」

translations.literal: When Shao reached Fengtian he was mixed with bandits filling moats; facing the city he suddenly greatly shouted, saying to those on the wall: "I am Li Huai'guang's envoy; Huai'guang from Hebei leads the great army and has arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shao reached Fengtian he was mixed with bandits filling moats. Facing the city he suddenly greatly shouted, saying to those on the wall, "I am Li Huai'guang's envoy. Huai'guang from Hebei leads the great army and has arrived!"

sentences.zh: 即繩引而登。

translations.literal: Then by rope he was drawn up and climbed.
translations.idiomatic: Then by rope he was drawn up and climbed.

sentences.zh: 城中得懷光表，歡聲振動，賊眾不之測，乃令舁韶巡於城上。

translations.literal: In the city they got Huai'guang's report; shouts shook; bandit masses could not measure it; they then ordered Shao carried on a tour of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the city they got Li Huai'guang's report. Shouts shook. Bandit masses could not measure it. They then ordered Zhang Shao carried on a tour of the wall.

sentences.zh: 翌日，懷光大軍次醴泉，是夜，賊解圍而去。

translations.literal: The next day Huai'guang's great army halted at Liquan; that night bandits lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Li Huai'guang's great army halted at Liquan. That night bandits lifted the siege and left.

sentences.zh: 興元元年正月，以瑊為行在都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xingyuan he was made mobile-court commander knowing troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Xingyuan he was made mobile-court commander knowing troops.

sentences.zh: 二月，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: In the second month he was given five hundred households of real enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was given five hundred households of real enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 是月，德宗移幸山南。

translations.literal: That month Dezong moved favor to Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: That month Emperor Dezong moved favor to Shannan.

sentences.zh: 時懷光叛逆，二賊連結，寇盜縱橫，瑊分布諸軍，以為翼衛，才入谷口，而懷光追騎遽至，瑊令侯仲莊以後軍擊敗之。

translations.literal: At that time Huai'guang rebelled; the two bandits linked; bandits and robbers ran wild; Jian distributed the armies as wing guards; just entering the valley mouth Huai'guang's pursuit cavalry suddenly arrived; Jian ordered Hou Zhongzhuang with the rear army to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Huai'guang rebelled. The two bandits linked. Bandits and robbers ran wild. Jian distributed the armies as wing guards. Just entering the valley mouth Huai'guang's pursuit cavalry suddenly arrived. Jian ordered Hou Zhongzhuang with the rear army to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 三月，加檢校左僕射、同中書門下平章事，兼靈州都督、靈鹽豐夏等州、定遠西城天德軍節度等使，仍充朔方邠寧振武等道兼永平軍奉天行營兵馬副元帥，上臨軒授鉞，用漢拜韓信故事。

translations.literal: In the third month he was promoted acting Left Vice Director, concurrent Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, concurrently Ling Prefecture governor, Ling-Yan-Feng-Xia and other prefectures, Dingyuan West City and Tiande Army military commissioner and others, still deputy grand marshal of Shuofang, Binning, Zhenwu and other routes and Yongping Army Fengtian mobile-camp troops; the emperor at the hall steps granted the axe—using the Han precedent of enfeoffing Han Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was promoted acting Left Vice Director, concurrent Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, concurrently Ling Prefecture governor, Ling-Yan-Feng-Xia and other prefectures, Dingyuan West City and Tiande Army military commissioner and others, still deputy grand marshal of Shuofang, Binning, Zhenwu and other routes and Yongping Army Fengtian mobile-camp troops. The emperor at the hall steps granted the axe—using the Han precedent of enfeoffing Han Xin.

sentences.zh: 是月，瑊將諸軍赴京畿，賊將韓旻、張廷芝、宋歸朝等拒我師於武功，瑊與吐蕃將論莽羅之眾大破賊於武亭川，斬首萬余級。

translations.literal: That month Jian led the armies to go to Jingji; bandit generals Han Min, Zhang Tingzhi, Song Guichao and others resisted our army at Wugong; Jian with Tibetan general Lun Mangluo's masses greatly broke the bandits at Wuting River and cut off more than ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jian led the armies to go to Jingji. Bandit generals Han Min, Zhang Tingzhi, Song Guichao and others resisted our army at Wugong. Jian with Tibetan general Lun Mangluo's masses greatly broke the bandits at Wuting River and cut off more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 瑊便赴奉天應接李晟，抗京城西面。

translations.literal: Jian then went to Fengtian to respond to Li Sheng and resisted the capital's west face.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then went to Fengtian to respond to Li Sheng and resisted the capital's west face.

sentences.zh: 五月，李晟自東渭橋抵京城攻賊，瑊亦與韓遊瑰、戴休顏西面諸軍會合。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Li Sheng from East Wei Bridge reached the capital to attack bandits; Jian also with Han Yougui, Dai Xiuyan and western face armies joined.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Li Sheng from East Wei Bridge reached the capital to attack bandits. Jian also with Han Yougui, Dai Xiuyan and western face armies joined.

sentences.zh: 晟破賊之日，瑊亦進收咸陽。

translations.literal: The day Sheng broke the bandits Jian also advanced and recovered Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: The day Li Sheng broke the bandits Jian also advanced and recovered Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 尋聞硃泚、姚令言奔敗，命諸軍分道邀擊，其眾離潰，相率來降。

translations.literal: Soon hearing Zhu Ci and Yao Lingyan fled in defeat he ordered the armies to divide routes intercept; their masses scattered and fled and in succession came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Soon hearing Zhu Ci and Yao Lingyan fled in defeat he ordered the armies to divide routes intercept. Their masses scattered and fled and in succession came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 選勁騎三千急追泚至涇州，賊將誅泚，傳首來獻。

translations.literal: He selected three thousand strong cavalry urgently pursuing Ci to Jing Prefecture; bandit generals executed Ci and sent the head to present.
translations.idiomatic: He selected three thousand strong cavalry urgently pursuing Zhu Ci to Jing Prefecture. Bandit generals executed Ci and sent the head to present.

sentences.zh: 六月，加瑊侍中。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Jian was promoted Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Jian was promoted Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 論收京城之功，加實封李晟一千戶，瑊八百戶，韓遊瑰、戴休顏四百戶，駱元光、尚可孤五百戶。

translations.literal: Discussing merit in recovering the capital Li Sheng was given one thousand households of real enfeoffment, Jian eight hundred, Han Yougui and Dai Xiuyan four hundred, Luo Yuanguang and Shang Kehu five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Discussing merit in recovering the capital Li Sheng was given one thousand households of real enfeoffment, Jian eight hundred, Han Yougui and Dai Xiuyan four hundred, Luo Yuanguang and Shang Kehu five hundred.

sentences.zh: 七月，德宗還宮，以瑊守本官，兼河中尹、河中絳慈隰節度使，仍充河中同陜虢節度及管內諸軍行營兵馬副元帥，改封咸寧郡王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Dezong returned to the palace; Jian kept his original office, concurrently Hedong governor, Hedong-Jiang-Ci-Xi military commissioner, still deputy grand marshal of Hedong-Tong-Shaan-Guo military commission and circuit internal mobile-camp troops, changed enfeoffment Prince of Xianning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Emperor Dezong returned to the palace. Jian kept his original office, concurrently Hedong governor, Hedong-Jiang-Ci-Xi military commissioner, still deputy grand marshal of Hedong-Tong-Shaan-Guo military commission and circuit internal mobile-camp troops, changed enfeoffment Prince of Xianning Commandery.

sentences.zh: 九月，賜瑊大寧裏甲第、女樂五人，入第之日，宰臣、節將送之，一如李晟入第之儀。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jian was given a mansion in Daning Lane and five singing girls; the day he entered the mansion ministers and military commissioners escorted him—just like Li Sheng's mansion entry ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jian was given a mansion in Daning Lane and five singing girls. The day he entered the mansion ministers and military commissioners escorted him—just like Li Sheng's mansion entry ceremony.

sentences.zh: 以李懷光未平，又加朔方行營兵馬副元帥，與河東節度使馬燧會兵進討。

translations.literal: Because Li Huai'guang was not yet pacified he was again made Shuofang mobile-camp troops deputy grand marshal and joined Hedong military commissioner Ma Sui in armies to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Huai'guang was not yet pacified he was again made Shuofang mobile-camp troops deputy grand marshal and joined Hedong military commissioner Ma Sui in armies to advance and attack.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年八月，河中平，以功加檢校司空，與一子五品正員官。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhenyuan Hedong was pacified; for merit he was promoted acting Minister of Works and one son fifth-rank regular office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhenyuan Hedong was pacified. For merit he was promoted acting Minister of Works and one son fifth-rank regular office.

sentences.zh: 是冬望，皇帝親郊昊天上帝，瑊入朝陪祀畢，還鎮河中。

translations.literal: That winter solstice the emperor personally sacrificed to August Heaven at the suburban altar; Jian entered court accompanying the sacrifice and then returned to garrison Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice the emperor personally sacrificed to August Heaven at the suburban altar. Jian entered court accompanying the sacrifice and then returned to garrison Hedong.

sentences.zh: 三年，吐蕃入寇，至鳳翔，為李晟邀擊之，又襲破其摧沙堡，吐蕃深恨之。

translations.literal: In the third year Tibet entered to raid and reached Fengxiang; Li Sheng intercepted them and again raided and broke their Cuisha Fort; Tibet deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Tibet entered to raid and reached Fengxiang. Li Sheng intercepted them and again raided and broke their Cuisha Fort. Tibet deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 尚結贊入寇，陷我鹽、夏二州，以兵守之。

translations.literal: Shang Jiezan entered to raid and took our Yan and Xia prefectures and held them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Jiezan entered to raid and took our Yan and Xia prefectures and held them with troops.

sentences.zh: 欲長驅犯京師，而畏瑊與李晟、馬燧，欲陰計圖之。

translations.literal: He wished to drive straight to violate the capital yet feared Jian and Li Sheng and Ma Sui; he wished secretly by plan to scheme against them.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to drive straight to violate the capital yet feared Jian and Li Sheng and Ma Sui. He wished secretly by plan to scheme against them.

sentences.zh: 乃卑詞遜禮告馬燧，請重立盟誓，則蕃軍引去，德宗不許。

translations.literal: He then with humble words and yielding courtesy told Ma Sui, asking to renew alliance oaths; then Tibetan troops would withdraw; Dezong did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He then with humble words and yielding courtesy told Ma Sui, asking to renew alliance oaths. Then Tibetan troops would withdraw. Emperor Dezong did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 馬燧自入朝言之，上乃令崔翰入蕃報結贊，言還我鹽、夏，則許同盟。

translations.literal: Ma Sui from entering court spoke of it; the emperor then ordered Cui Han to enter Tibet to report to Jiezan, saying return our Yan and Xia and then grant joint alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui from entering court spoke of it. The emperor then ordered Cui Han to enter Tibet to report to Jiezan, saying return our Yan and Xia and then grant joint alliance.

sentences.zh: 結贊謂翰曰：「清水之會，同盟人少，是以和好輕慢不成；

translations.literal: Jiezan said to Han: "At the Qingshui meeting allied men were few; therefore good relations were lightly treated and did not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan said to Cui Han, "At the Qingshui meeting allied men were few. Therefore good relations were lightly treated and did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 今蕃相及元帥已下凡二十一人赴盟，靈州節度使杜希全、涇原節度使李觀皆和善守信，境外重之，此時須請預盟。」

translations.literal: now the Tibetan minister and grand marshal and below total twenty-one men go to alliance; Ling Prefecture military commissioner Du Xiquan and Jingyuan military commissioner Li Guan are all good-natured and keep faith, heavily regarded beyond the borders—at this time one must request they pre-join the alliance."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Tibetan minister and grand marshal and below total twenty-one men go to alliance. Ling Prefecture military commissioner Du Xiquan and Jingyuan military commissioner Li Guan are all good-natured and keep faith, heavily regarded beyond the borders—at this time one must request they pre-join the alliance."

sentences.zh: 翰約盟於清水，且先歸我鹽、夏二州，結贊曰：「清水非吉地，請會盟於原州土梨樹。」

translations.literal: Han arranged alliance at Qingshui and first return our Yan and Xia two prefectures; Jiezan said: "Qingshui is not an auspicious place; please meet alliance at Yuan Prefecture Tulishu."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Han arranged alliance at Qingshui and first return our Yan and Xia two prefectures. Jiezan said, "Qingshui is not an auspicious place. Please meet alliance at Yuan Prefecture Tulishu."

sentences.zh: 又請盟畢歸二州。

translations.literal: He again asked after alliance finish to return the two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked after alliance finish to return the two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 翰歸，備奏其事，神策將馬有麟奏曰：「土梨樹地多險，恐蕃軍隱伏不利，不如於平涼，其地坦平，且近涇州，就之為便。」

translations.literal: Han returned and fully reported the matter; Shence general Ma Youlin memorialized: "Tulishu ground has much peril; fear Tibetan troops hidden in ambush unfavorable; better at Pingliang—the ground is level and flat and near Jing Prefecture; going there is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Han returned and fully reported the matter. Shence general Ma Youlin memorialized, "Tulishu ground has much peril. Fear Tibetan troops hidden in ambush unfavorable. Better at Pingliang—the ground is level and flat and near Jing Prefecture. Going there is convenient."

sentences.zh: 乃定盟於平涼川。

translations.literal: They then fixed alliance at Pingliang River.
translations.idiomatic: They then fixed alliance at Pingliang River.

sentences.zh: 初，結贊請李觀、杜希全預盟，欲執之，徑犯京師。

translations.literal: At first Jiezan requested Li Guan and Du Xiquan pre-join the alliance intending to seize them and straight violate the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At first Jiezan requested Li Guan and Du Xiquan pre-join the alliance intending to seize them and straight violate the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔報之曰：「杜希全職在靈州，不可出境，李觀又已改官；

translations.literal: An edict replied: "Du Xiquan's duty is at Ling Prefecture and he cannot leave the border; Li Guan has already changed office;
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "Du Xiquan's duty is at Ling Prefecture and he cannot leave the border. Li Guan has already changed office.

sentences.zh: 今遣侍中渾瑊充盟會使。」

translations.literal: now dispatch Palace Attendant Hun Jian as alliance meeting envoy."
translations.idiomatic: Now dispatch Palace Attendant Hun Jian as alliance meeting envoy."

sentences.zh: 五月，瑊自咸陽入朝，詔授平涼盟會使，兵部尚書崔漢衡副之，司勛郎中鄭叔矩為判官。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Jian from Xianyang entered court; an edict appointed Pingliang alliance envoy; Minister of War Cui Hanheng deputy; Director of Merits Bureau Zheng Shuju judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Jian from Xianyang entered court. An edict appointed Pingliang alliance envoy. Minister of War Cui Hanheng deputy. Director of Merits Bureau Zheng Shuju judge.

sentences.zh: 瑊統兵二萬，又詔華州節度使駱元光以本鎮兵從瑊。

translations.literal: Jian commanded twenty thousand troops; an edict again ordered Hua Prefecture military commissioner Luo Yuanguang with his garrison troops follow Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Jian commanded twenty thousand troops. An edict again ordered Hua Prefecture military commissioner Luo Yuanguang with his garrison troops follow Jian.

sentences.zh: 閏月十五日，瑊與結贊會平涼。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the intercalary month Jian and Jiezan met at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the intercalary month Jian and Jiezan met at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 初，約以兵三千列於壇之東西，散手四百人至壇下，各遣遊軍相覘伺。

translations.literal: At first they agreed three thousand troops array east and west of the altar; four hundred unarmed men to below the altar; each side dispatch roaming troops to observe.
translations.idiomatic: At first they agreed three thousand troops array east and west of the altar. Four hundred unarmed men to below the altar. Each side dispatch roaming troops to observe.

sentences.zh: 是時，蕃軍精騎數萬列於壇西，蕃之遊軍貫穿我軍之中。
