translations.literal: At that time Tibetan elite cavalry numbering tens of thousands arrayed west of the altar; Tibetan roaming troops pierced through our army's center.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tibetan elite cavalry numbering tens of thousands arrayed west of the altar. Tibetan roaming troops pierced through our army's center.

sentences.zh: 瑊將梁奉貞率六十騎為遊軍，才至壇所，為蕃軍所執。

translations.literal: Jian's general Liang Fengzhen led sixty horsemen as roaming troops; just reaching the altar place they were seized by Tibetan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's general Liang Fengzhen led sixty horsemen as roaming troops. Just reaching the altar place they were seized by Tibetan troops.

sentences.zh: 結贊又謂瑊曰：「請侍中已下具衣冠劍珮。」

translations.literal: Jiezan again said to Jian: "Please Palace Attendant and below fully wear robes, caps, swords, and girdle pendants."
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan again said to Jian, "Please Palace Attendant and below fully wear robes, caps, swords, and girdle pendants."

sentences.zh: 瑊與監軍宋鳳朝、崔漢衡等入幕次，坦無他慮。

translations.literal: Jian with army supervisor Song Fengchao, Cui Hanheng and others entered the tent; open without other concern.
translations.idiomatic: Jian with army supervisor Song Fengchao, Cui Hanheng and others entered the tent, open without other concern.

sentences.zh: 結贊命伐鼓三通，其眾呼噪而至。

translations.literal: Jiezan ordered drums beaten three rounds; his masses shouting and clamoring arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezan ordered drums beaten three rounds. His masses shouting and clamoring arrived.

sentences.zh: 瑊遽出自幕後，偶得他馬，跨而奔馳，追騎雲合，流矢雨集而不傷。

translations.literal: Jian hastily came out from behind the tent; by chance he got another horse, straddled and galloped; pursuit cavalry clouded together; flowing arrows rained yet did not harm.
translations.idiomatic: Jian hastely came out from behind the tent. By chance he got another horse, straddled and galloped. Pursuit cavalry clouded together. Flowing arrows rained yet did not harm.

sentences.zh: 會瑊將辛榮以數百人入據北阜，與賊血戰，追騎方止，瑊僅得免，辛榮兵盡矢窮，力屈而降。

translations.literal: When Jian's general Xin Rong with several hundred men entered and held the north height fighting blood battle pursuit cavalry then stopped; Jian barely escaped; Xin Rong's troops exhausted arrows and strength bent and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian's general Xin Rong with several hundred men entered and held the north height fighting blood battle pursuit cavalry then stopped. Jian barely escaped. Xin Rong's troops exhausted arrows and strength bent and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 宋鳳朝、瑊判官鄭弇，為追兵所殺；

translations.literal: Song Fengchao and Jian's judge Zheng Yan were killed by pursuit troops;
translations.idiomatic: Song Fengchao and Jian's judge Zheng Yan were killed by pursuit troops.

sentences.zh: 崔漢衡、中官俱文珍、劉延、李清朝，漢衡判官鄭叔矩、瑊判官路泌、袁同直，大將軍扶余準、馬寧、神策將孟日華、李至言、樂演明、範澄、馬弇等六十余人，皆陷於賊。

translations.literal: Cui Hanheng, palace attendant Ju Wenzhen, Liu Yan, Li Qingchao, Hanheng's judge Zheng Shuju, Jian's judge Lu Bi, Yuan Tongzhi, great generals Fuyu Zhun, Ma Ning, Shence generals Meng Rihua, Li Zhiyan, Yue Yanming, Fan Cheng, Ma Yan and more than sixty others—all fell into bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hanheng, palace attendant Ju Wenzhen, Liu Yan, Li Qingchao, Hanheng's judge Zheng Shuju, Jian's judge Lu Bi, Yuan Tongzhi, great generals Fuyu Zhun, Ma Ning, Shence generals Meng Rihua, Li Zhiyan, Yue Yanming, Fan Cheng, Ma Yan and more than sixty others—all fell into bandits.

sentences.zh: 尚結贊至原州，列坐帳中，召陷蕃將吏讓之，因怒瑊曰：「武功之捷，吐蕃之力，許以涇州、靈州相報，竟食其言，負我深矣，舉國同怨。

translations.literal: Shang Jiezan reached Yuan Prefecture, sat in rows in the tent, summoned trapped-in-Tibet officers and clerks and blamed them; then angrily to Jian said: "The Wugong victory—Tibet's strength; promised Jing and Ling prefectures in return—ultimately ate their words; deeply wronged us; the whole state together resents.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Jiezan reached Yuan Prefecture, sat in rows in the tent, summoned trapped-in-Tibet officers and clerks and blamed them. Then angrily to Jian said, "The Wugong victory—Tibet's strength. Promised Jing and Ling prefectures in return—ultimately ate their words. Deeply wronged us. The whole state together resents.

sentences.zh: 本劫是盟，誌在擒瑊。

translations.literal: Originally robbing this alliance—the intent was to capture Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Originally robbing this alliance—the intent was to capture Jian.

sentences.zh: 吾已為金枷待瑊，將獻贊普；

translations.literal: I already made a golden cangue waiting for Jian to present to the tsenpo;
translations.idiomatic: I already made a golden cangue waiting for Jian to present to the tsenpo.

sentences.zh: 既已失之，虛致君等何為？」

translations.literal: already lost him—why in vain bring you all?"
translations.idiomatic: Already lost him—why in vain bring you all?"

sentences.zh: 乃放俱文珍、馬寧、馬弇歸朝。

translations.literal: He then released Ju Wenzhen, Ma Ning, and Ma Yan to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: He then released Ju Wenzhen, Ma Ning, and Ma Yan to return to court.

sentences.zh: 七月，瑊自奉天入朝，素服待罪，詔釋之而後見。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Jian from Fengtian entered court in plain clothes awaiting guilt; an edict released him and then he was seen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Jian from Fengtian entered court in plain clothes awaiting guilt. An edict released him and then he was seen.

sentences.zh: 俄而吐蕃入寇京畿，瑊鎮奉天。

translations.literal: Soon Tibet entered to raid Jingji; Jian garrisoned Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tibet entered to raid Jingji. Jian garrisoned Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 十月，還河中。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he returned to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he returned to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，加邠、寧、慶副元帥。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year he was made Bin-Ning-Qing deputy grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year he was made Bin-Ning-Qing deputy grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，加檢校司徒，兼中書令，諸使、副元帥如故。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year he was promoted acting Grand Mentor, concurrently Director of the Secretariat, all commissioners and deputy grand marshal as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year he was promoted acting Grand Mentor, concurrently Director of the Secretariat, all commissioners and deputy grand marshal as before.

sentences.zh: 十五年十二月二日，薨於鎮。

translations.literal: On the second day of the twelfth month of the fifteenth year he died at garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the twelfth month of the fifteenth year he died at garrison.

sentences.zh: 廢朝五日，群臣於延英奉慰。

translations.literal: Court mourning was suspended five days; ministers at Yanying offered condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning was suspended five days. Ministers at Yanying offered condolences.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太師，謚曰忠武，賻絹布四千匹、米粟三千石。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor with posthumous title Zhongwu; funeral gifts four thousand bolts of silk and cloth and three thousand shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor with posthumous title Zhongwu. Funeral gifts four thousand bolts of silk and cloth and three thousand shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 及喪車將至，又為廢朝。

translations.literal: When the funeral cart was about to arrive court mourning was again suspended.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral cart was about to arrive court mourning was again suspended.

sentences.zh: 應緣喪事，所司準式支給，命京兆尹監護。

translations.literal: For funeral affairs the responsible offices paid according to standard regulations; the emperor ordered the Capital Intendant to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: For funeral affairs the responsible offices paid according to standard regulations. The emperor ordered the Capital Intendant to supervise.

sentences.zh: 葬日，賜絹五百匹。

translations.literal: On burial day five hundred bolts of silk were granted.
translations.idiomatic: On burial day five hundred bolts of silk were granted.

sentences.zh: 瑊忠勤謹慎，功高不伐，在籓方歲時貢奉，必躬親閱視；

translations.literal: Jian was loyal, diligent, and careful; merit high yet not boastful; in the frontier each year when presenting tribute he must personally inspect;
translations.idiomatic: Jian was loyal, diligent, and careful. Merit high yet not boastful. In the frontier each year when presenting tribute he must personally inspect.

sentences.zh: 每有頒錫，雖居遠地，如在帝前。

translations.literal: whenever there were bestowals though dwelling far he was as before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there were bestowals though dwelling far he was as before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 位極將相，無忘謙抑，物論方之金日磾，故深為德宗委信，猜間不能入，君子多之。

translations.literal: Rank reaching general and minister he did not forget modest restraint; public opinion compared him to Jin Midi; therefore Dezong deeply entrusted him; suspicion could not enter; gentlemen praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Rank reaching general and minister he did not forget modest restraint. Public opinion compared him to Jin Midi. Therefore Emperor Dezong deeply entrusted him. Suspicion could not enter. Gentlemen praised him.

sentences.zh: 子練、鎬、鐬。

translations.literal: Sons Lian, Gao, and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Lian, Gao, and Hui.

sentences.zh: 鎬，瑊第二子。

translations.literal: Gao was Jian's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was Jian's second son.

sentences.zh: 性謙謹，多與士大夫遊。

translations.literal: Nature modest and careful; he often associated with scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Nature modest and careful. He often associated with scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 歷延、唐二州刺史，軍政吏職，有可稱者。

translations.literal: He served Yan and Tang prefectures; in military affairs, government, and official duties there were matters worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: He served Yan and Tang prefectures. In military affairs, government, and official duties there were matters worth praising.

sentences.zh: 及元和中，諸道出師討王承宗，屬義武軍節度使任迪簡病不能軍，以鎬藉父威名，足以鎮定，乃以鎬檢校右散騎常侍，充義武軍節度副使。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era the various routes sent out armies to attack Wang Chengzong; because Yiwu Army military commissioner Ren Dijian was ill and could not command the army, because Gao relied on his father's martial name sufficient to pacify and settle, Gao was made acting Right Regular Attendant and Yiwu Army military commission deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era the various routes sent out armies to attack Wang Chengzong. Because Yiwu Army military commissioner Ren Dijian was ill and could not command the army, because Gao relied on his father's martial name sufficient to pacify and settle, Gao was made acting Right Regular Attendant and Yiwu Army military commission deputy.

sentences.zh: 九月六日，加檢校工部尚書，代迪簡為節度使。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the ninth month he was promoted acting Minister of Works replacing Dijian as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the ninth month he was promoted acting Minister of Works replacing Ren Dijian as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鎬治兵練卒，頗有威望，然不能觀釁養銳，以期必勝。

translations.literal: Gao trained troops and drilled soldiers and had considerable prestige, yet he could not watch for openings and nurture sharpness awaiting sure victory.
translations.idiomatic: Gao trained troops and drilled soldiers and had considerable prestige, yet he could not watch for openings and nurture sharpness awaiting sure victory.

sentences.zh: 鎮、定相去九十里，元和十一年冬，鎬率全師壓賊境而軍，距賊壘三十里。

translations.literal: Zhen and Ding were ninety li apart; in the winter of the eleventh year of Yuanhe Gao led the whole army pressing the bandit border and encamped thirty li from the bandit camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Ding were ninety li apart. In the winter of the eleventh year of Yuanhe Gao led the whole army pressing the bandit border and encamped thirty li from the bandit camp.

sentences.zh: 鎬謀慮不周，但耀兵鋒，無所控制，賊乃分兵潛入定州界焚燒驅掠。

translations.literal: Gao's plans were not thorough; he only displayed martial points without any control; bandits then divided troops secretly entering Ding Prefecture circuit burning, driving, and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's plans were not thorough. He only displayed martial points without any control. Bandits then divided troops secretly entering Ding Prefecture circuit burning, driving, and plundering.

sentences.zh: 鎬怒，進攻賊壘，交鋒而敗，師徒殆喪其半，余眾還定州，亂不可遏，朝廷乃除陳楚代之。

translations.literal: Gao was angry and advanced to attack the bandit camp; crossing blades he was defeated; army and troops nearly lost half; remaining masses returned to Ding Prefecture; chaos could not be checked; the court then removed Chen Chu to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was angry and advanced to attack the bandit camp. Crossing blades he was defeated. Army and troops nearly lost half. Remaining masses returned to Ding Prefecture. Chaos could not be checked. The court then removed Chen Chu to replace him.

sentences.zh: 楚聞亂，馳入定州。

translations.literal: Chu hearing of the chaos galloped into Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chu hearing of the chaos galloped into Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鎬為亂兵所劫，以至裸露。

translations.literal: Gao was robbed by mutinous troops even to nakedness.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was robbed by mutinous troops even to nakedness.

sentences.zh: 楚既整戢，於亂兵處率斂衣服還鎬，方得歸朝，坐貶韶州刺史。

translations.literal: Once Chu had restored order at the mutinous troops' place he gathered clothes and returned them to Gao; only then could he return to court; he was demoted Sha Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chen Chu had restored order at the mutinous troops' place he gathered clothes and returned them to Gao. Only then could he return to court. He was demoted Sha Prefecture prefect.

sentences.zh: 後代州刺史韓重華奏收得鎬供軍錢絹十余萬貫匹，再貶循州刺史。

translations.literal: Later replacing Dai Prefecture prefect Han Chonghua memorialized recovering Gao's army supply money and silk more than one hundred thousand strings and bolts; he was again demoted Xun Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Later replacing Dai Prefecture prefect Han Chonghua memorialized recovering Gao's army supply money and silk more than one hundred thousand strings and bolts. He was again demoted Xun Prefecture prefect.

sentences.zh: 歲余卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he died.

sentences.zh: 鐬，瑊第三子，以廕起家為諸衛參軍，歷諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: Hui was Jian's third son; through shadow privilege he began as various guard adjutant; he served various guard generals.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was Jian's third son. Through shadow privilege he began as various guard adjutant. He served various guard generals.

sentences.zh: 元和初，出為豐州刺史、天德軍使，坐贓貶袁州司戶，憲宗思咸寧之勛，比例從輕。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanhe he went out as Feng Prefecture prefect and Tiande Army commander; because of corruption he was demoted Yuan Prefecture registrar; Emperor Xianzong thought of Xianning's merit and proportionally lightened from the norm.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhe he went out as Feng Prefecture prefect and Tiande Army commander. Because of corruption he was demoted Yuan Prefecture registrar. Emperor Xianzong thought of Xianning's merit and proportionally lightened from the norm.

sentences.zh: 五年，征為袁王傅，復賜金紫，遷殿中監。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned as Yuan King's tutor; again given gold and purple; promoted Director of the Palace Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was summoned as Yuan King's tutor. Again given gold and purple. Promoted Director of the Palace Directorate.

sentences.zh: 開成初，宰相擬壽州刺史，文宗曰：「鐬，勛臣子弟，豈可委以牧民？

translations.literal: At the start of Kaicheng the chief ministers proposed Shou Prefecture prefect; Emperor Wenzong said: "Hui is a meritorious minister's son—how can he be entrusted with governing the people?
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaicheng the chief ministers proposed Shou Prefecture prefect. Emperor Wenzong said, "Hui is a meritorious minister's son—how can he be entrusted with governing the people?

sentences.zh: 仲尼有言，『不如多與之邑』，今我念其先人之功，與之致富可也。」

translations.literal: Confucius had a saying, 'Better give him many towns,'—now I think of his forebear's merit; giving him wealth is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius had a saying, 'Better give him many towns'—now I think of his forebear's merit. Giving him wealth is enough."

sentences.zh: 宰臣曰：「鐬常歷名郡，有政能。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers said: "Hui often served famous prefectures and had governmental ability."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers said, "Hui often served famous prefectures and had governmental ability."

sentences.zh: 乃從之。

translations.literal: They then followed it.
translations.idiomatic: They then followed it.

sentences.zh: 三年，入為右金吾衛大將軍、知街事，歷諸衛大將軍，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered as Right Golden Guard great general knowing street affairs; he served various guard great generals and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he entered as Right Golden Guard great general knowing street affairs. He served various guard great generals and died.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：馬司徒之方略，渾咸寧之忠藎，各奮節義，為時名臣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Minister Ma's stratagem and Xianning's loyalty and devotion each exerted integrity and righteousness and were famed ministers of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Minister Ma's stratagem and Xianning's loyalty and devotion each exerted integrity and righteousness and were famed ministers of the age.

sentences.zh: 然元城之師，失策於田悅；

translations.literal: Yet at Yuancheng's army he lost plan against Tian Yue;
translations.idiomatic: Yet at Yuancheng's army he lost plan against Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 平涼之會，幾陷於吐蕃，此亦術有所不至也。

translations.literal: at the Pingliang meeting he nearly fell into Tibet—this too is where skill did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: At the Pingliang meeting he nearly fell into Tibet—this too is where skill did not reach.

sentences.zh: 緬思建中之亂，四海波騰，賊泚竊發之辰，宗祀不絕如線，茍非忠臣致命，化危為安，則李氏之宗社傾矣。

translations.literal: Looking back on Jianzhong's chaos when the four seas surged and bandit Ci secretly rose when the ancestral temple was unbroken like a thread—if not for loyal ministers giving their lives, transforming peril to peace, then the Li clan's altars would have toppled.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on Jianzhong's chaos when the four seas surged and bandit Zhu Ci secretly rose when the ancestral temple was unbroken like a thread—if not for loyal ministers giving their lives, transforming peril to peace, then the Li clan's altars would have toppled.

sentences.zh: 贊

translations.literal: Eulogy
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy

sentences.zh: 贊曰：北平之勛，排難解紛。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Beiping's merit—removing difficulty, resolving strife.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Beiping's merit—removing difficulty, resolving strife.

sentences.zh: 咸寧蹈義，感慨匡君。

translations.literal: Xianning treading righteousness—stirred to emotion, aiding the lord.
translations.idiomatic: Xianning treading righteousness—stirred to emotion, aiding the lord.

sentences.zh: 再隆基構，克殄昏氛。

translations.literal: Again raising the imperial enterprise—utterly extinguishing murky vapors.
translations.idiomatic: Again raising the imperial enterprise—utterly extinguishing murky vapors.

sentences.zh: 回天捧日，實賴將軍。

translations.literal: Turning back Heaven, upholding the sun—truly relying on the general.
translations.idiomatic: Turning back Heaven, upholding the sun—truly relying on the general.
